draft_translation: And he said to them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for this reason I was sent.
ukjv_translation: And he said unto them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.

greek_text: και ην κηρυσσων εν ταις συναγωγαις της γαλιλαιας
transliteration: kai hn khrusswn en taiv sunagwgaiv thv galilaiav
draft_translation: And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.
ukjv_translation: And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: εγενετο δε εν τω τον οχλον επικεισθαι αυτω του ακουειν τον λογον του θεου και αυτος ην εστως παρα την λιμνην γεννησαρετ
transliteration: egeneto de en tw ton oclon epikeisyai autw tou akouein ton logon tou yeou kai autov hn estwv para thn limnhn gennhsaret
draft_translation: And it happened, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word (o. logos) of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,

greek_text: και ειδεν δυο πλοια εστωτα παρα την λιμνην οι δε αλιεις αποβαντες απ αυτων απεπλυναν τα δικτυα
transliteration: kai eiden duo ploia estwta para thn limnhn oi de alieiv apobantev ap autwn apeplunan ta diktua
draft_translation: And saw two boats standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
ukjv_translation: And saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.

greek_text: εμβας δε εις εν των πλοιων ο ην του σιμωνος ηρωτησεν αυτον απο της γης επαναγαγειν ολιγον και καθισας εδιδασκεν εκ του πλοιου τους οχλους
transliteration: embav de eiv en twn ploiwn o hn tou simwnov hrwthsen auton apo thv ghv epanagagein oligon kai kayisav edidasken ek tou ploiou touv oclouv
draft_translation: And he entered into one of the boats, which was Simon's, and asked him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the boat.
ukjv_translation: And he entered into one of the ships, which was Simon's, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship.
review_notes: fixed prayed-him relative artifact; modernized him-that relative; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: ως δε επαυσατο λαλων ειπεν προς τον σιμωνα επαναγαγε εις το βαθος και χαλασατε τα δικτυα υμων εις αγραν
transliteration: wv de epausato lalwn eipen prov ton simwna epanagage eiv to bayov kai calasate ta diktua umwn eiv agran
draft_translation: Now when he had left speaking, he said to Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch.
ukjv_translation: Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; rendered draught as catch

greek_text: και αποκριθεις ο σιμων ειπεν αυτω επιστατα δι ολης της νυκτος κοπιασαντες ουδεν ελαβομεν επι δε τω ρηματι σου χαλασω το δικτυον
transliteration: kai apokriyeiv o simwn eipen autw epistata di olhv thv nuktov kopiasantev ouden elabomen epi de tw rhmati sou calasw to diktuon
draft_translation: And Simon answering said to him, Master, we have toiled all night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at your word I will let down the net.
ukjv_translation: And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at your word (o. rhema) I will let down the net.

greek_text: και τουτο ποιησαντες συνεκλεισαν ιχθυων πληθος πολυ διερρηγνυτο δε το δικτυον αυτων
transliteration: kai touto poihsantev sunekleisan icyuwn plhyov polu dierrhgnuto de to diktuon autwn
draft_translation: And when they had this done, they enclosed a great multitude of fish: and their net broke.
ukjv_translation: And when they had this done, they enclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake.
review_notes: modernized brake as broke; modernized fishes plural

greek_text: και κατενευσαν τοις μετοχοις τοις εν τω ετερω πλοιω του ελθοντας συλλαβεσθαι αυτοις και ηλθον και επλησαν αμφοτερα τα πλοια ωστε βυθιζεσθαι αυτα
transliteration: kai kateneusan toiv metocoiv toiv en tw eterw ploiw tou elyontav sullabesyai autoiv kai hlyon kai eplhsan amfotera ta ploia wste buyizesyai auta
draft_translation: And they beckoned to their partners, who were in the other boat, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the boats, so that they began to sink.
ukjv_translation: And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.

greek_text: ιδων δε σιμων πετρος προσεπεσεν τοις γονασιν του ιησου λεγων εξελθε απ εμου οτι ανηρ αμαρτωλος ειμι κυριε
transliteration: idwn de simwn petrov prosepesen toiv gonasin tou ihsou legwn exelye ap emou oti anhr amartwlov eimi kurie
draft_translation: When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
ukjv_translation: When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.

greek_text: θαμβος γαρ περιεσχεν αυτον και παντας τους συν αυτω επι τη αγρα των ιχθυων η συνελαβον
transliteration: yambov gar periescen auton kai pantav touv sun autw epi th agra twn icyuwn h sunelabon
draft_translation: For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the catch of fish which they had taken:
ukjv_translation: For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken:
review_notes: modernized fishes plural; rendered draught as catch

greek_text: ομοιως δε και ιακωβον και ιωαννην υιους ζεβεδαιου οι ησαν κοινωνοι τω σιμωνι και ειπεν προς τον σιμωνα ο ιησους μη φοβου απο του νυν ανθρωπους εση ζωγρων
transliteration: omoiwv de kai iakwbon kai iwannhn uiouv zebedaiou oi hsan koinwnoi tw simwni kai eipen prov ton simwna o ihsouv mh fobou apo tou nun anyrwpouv esh zwgrwn
draft_translation: And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, do not fear; from now on you shall catch men.
ukjv_translation: And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth you shall catch men.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized fear-not imperative; modernized from-henceforth idiom

greek_text: και καταγαγοντες τα πλοια επι την γην αφεντες απαντα ηκολουθησαν αυτω
transliteration: kai katagagontev ta ploia epi thn ghn afentev apanta hkolouyhsan autw
draft_translation: And when they had brought their boats to land, they left all, and followed him.
ukjv_translation: And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.

greek_text: και εγενετο εν τω ειναι αυτον εν μια των πολεων και ιδου ανηρ πληρης λεπρας και ιδων τον ιησουν πεσων επι προσωπον εδεηθη αυτου λεγων κυριε εαν θελης δυνασαι με καθαρισαι
transliteration: kai egeneto en tw einai auton en mia twn polewn kai idou anhr plhrhv leprav kai idwn ton ihsoun peswn epi proswpon edehyh autou legwn kurie ean yelhv dunasai me kayarisai
draft_translation: And it happened, when he was in a certain city, look a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on his face, and begged him, saying, Lord, if you will, you can make me clean.
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if you will, you can make me clean.
review_notes: modernized behold; modernized besought; modernized came-to-pass idiom; normalized NT kurios as Lord

greek_text: και εκτεινας την χειρα ηψατο αυτου ειπων θελω καθαρισθητι και ευθεως η λεπρα απηλθεν απ αυτου
transliteration: kai ekteinav thn ceira hqato autou eipwn yelw kayarisyhti kai euyewv h lepra aphlyen ap autou
draft_translation: And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.
ukjv_translation: And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be you clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.

greek_text: και αυτος παρηγγειλεν αυτω μηδενι ειπειν αλλα απελθων δειξον σεαυτον τω ιερει και προσενεγκε περι του καθαρισμου σου καθως προσεταξεν μωσης εις μαρτυριον αυτοις
transliteration: kai autov parhggeilen autw mhdeni eipein alla apelywn deixon seauton tw ierei kai prosenegke peri tou kayarismou sou kaywv prosetaxen mwshv eiv marturion autoiv
draft_translation: And he charged him to tell no one: but go, and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.
ukjv_translation: And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

greek_text: διηρχετο δε μαλλον ο λογος περι αυτου και συνηρχοντο οχλοι πολλοι ακουειν και θεραπευεσθαι υπ αυτου απο των ασθενειων αυτων
transliteration: dihrceto de mallon o logov peri autou kai sunhrconto ocloi polloi akouein kai yerapeuesyai up autou apo twn asyeneiwn autwn
draft_translation: But so much the more a report of him went out: and great crowds came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
ukjv_translation: But so much the more went there a fame (o. logos) abroad of him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
review_notes: modernized abroad idiom; removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker; rendered ochlos as crowd

greek_text: αυτος δε ην υποχωρων εν ταις ερημοις και προσευχομενος
transliteration: autov de hn upocwrwn en taiv erhmoiv kai proseucomenov
draft_translation: And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.
ukjv_translation: And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.

greek_text: και εγενετο εν μια των ημερων και αυτος ην διδασκων και ησαν καθημενοι φαρισαιοι και νομοδιδασκαλοι οι ησαν εληλυθοτες εκ πασης κωμης της γαλιλαιας και ιουδαιας και ιερουσαλημ και δυναμις κυριου ην εις το ιασθαι αυτους
transliteration: kai egeneto en mia twn hmerwn kai autov hn didaskwn kai hsan kayhmenoi farisaioi kai nomodidaskaloi oi hsan elhluyotev ek pashv kwmhv thv galilaiav kai ioudaiav kai ierousalhm kai dunamiv kuriou hn eiv to iasyai autouv
draft_translation: And it happened on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, who had come out of every town of Galilee, and Judea, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, which were come out of every town of Galilee, and Judaea, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
review_notes: modernized came-to-pass idiom; modernized personal which as who; modernized were-come perfect; normalized NT kurios as Lord; standardized Judea spelling

greek_text: και ιδου ανδρες φεροντες επι κλινης ανθρωπον ος ην παραλελυμενος και εζητουν αυτον εισενεγκειν και θειναι ενωπιον αυτου
transliteration: kai idou andrev ferontev epi klinhv anyrwpon ov hn paralelumenov kai ezhtoun auton eisenegkein kai yeinai enwpion autou
draft_translation: And, look, men brought on a bed a man who was paralyzed: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
ukjv_translation: And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.

greek_text: και μη ευροντες δια ποιας εισενεγκωσιν αυτον δια τον οχλον αναβαντες επι το δωμα δια των κεραμων καθηκαν αυτον συν τω κλινιδιω εις το μεσον εμπροσθεν του ιησου
transliteration: kai mh eurontev dia poiav eisenegkwsin auton dia ton oclon anabantev epi to dwma dia twn keramwn kayhkan auton sun tw klinidiw eiv to meson emprosyen tou ihsou
draft_translation: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the crowd, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiles with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
ukjv_translation: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.

greek_text: και ιδων την πιστιν αυτων ειπεν αυτω ανθρωπε αφεωνται σοι αι αμαρτιαι σου
transliteration: kai idwn thn pistin autwn eipen autw anyrwpe afewntai soi ai amartiai sou
draft_translation: And when he saw their faith, he said to him, Man, your sins are forgiven you.
ukjv_translation: And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, your sins are forgiven you.

greek_text: και ηρξαντο διαλογιζεσθαι οι γραμματεις και οι φαρισαιοι λεγοντες τις εστιν ουτος ος λαλει βλασφημιας τις δυναται αφιεναι αμαρτιας ει μη μονος ο θεος
transliteration: kai hrxanto dialogizesyai oi grammateiv kai oi farisaioi legontev tiv estin outov ov lalei blasfhmiav tiv dunatai afienai amartiav ei mh monov o yeov
draft_translation: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
ukjv_translation: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?

greek_text: επιγνους δε ο ιησους τους διαλογισμους αυτων αποκριθεις ειπεν προς αυτους τι διαλογιζεσθε εν ταις καρδιαις υμων
transliteration: epignouv de o ihsouv touv dialogismouv autwn apokriyeiv eipen prov autouv ti dialogizesye en taiv kardiaiv umwn
draft_translation: But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said to them, Why do you reason in your hearts?
ukjv_translation: But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said unto them, What reason all of you in your hearts?

greek_text: τι εστιν ευκοπωτερον ειπειν αφεωνται σοι αι αμαρτιαι σου η ειπειν εγειραι και περιπατει
transliteration: ti estin eukopwteron eipein afewntai soi ai amartiai sou h eipein egeirai kai peripatei
draft_translation: Which is easier, to say, Your sins are forgiven you; or to say, Rise up and walk?
ukjv_translation: Whether is easier, to say, Your sins be forgiven you; or to say, Rise up and walk?

greek_text: ινα δε ειδητε οτι εξουσιαν εχει ο υιος του ανθρωπου επι της γης αφιεναι αμαρτιας ειπεν τω παραλελυμενω σοι λεγω εγειραι και αρας το κλινιδιον σου πορευου εις τον οικον σου
transliteration: ina de eidhte oti exousian ecei o uiov tou anyrwpou epi thv ghv afienai amartiav eipen tw paralelumenw soi legw egeirai kai arav to klinidion sou poreuou eiv ton oikon sou
draft_translation: But that you may know that the Son of man has power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said to the sick with paralysis,) I say to you, Arise, and take up your couch, and go into your house.
ukjv_translation: But that all of you may know that the Son of man has power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto you, Arise, and take up your couch, and go into yours house.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized palsy; modernized sick-of wording; modernized yours before noun; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: και παραχρημα αναστας ενωπιον αυτων αρας εφ ω κατεκειτο απηλθεν εις τον οικον αυτου δοξαζων τον θεον
transliteration: kai paracrhma anastav enwpion autwn arav ef w katekeito aphlyen eiv ton oikon autou doxazwn ton yeon
draft_translation: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that on which he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.
ukjv_translation: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.

greek_text: και εκστασις ελαβεν απαντας και εδοξαζον τον θεον και επλησθησαν φοβου λεγοντες οτι ειδομεν παραδοξα σημερον
transliteration: kai ekstasiv elaben apantav kai edoxazon ton yeon kai eplhsyhsan fobou legontev oti eidomen paradoxa shmeron
draft_translation: And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen remarkable things today.
ukjv_translation: And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to day.

greek_text: και μετα ταυτα εξηλθεν και εθεασατο τελωνην ονοματι λευιν καθημενον επι το τελωνιον και ειπεν αυτω ακολουθει μοι
transliteration: kai meta tauta exhlyen kai eyeasato telwnhn onomati leuin kayhmenon epi to telwnion kai eipen autw akolouyei moi
draft_translation: And after these things he went forth, and saw a tax collector, named Levi, sitting at the tax booth: and he said to him, Follow me.
ukjv_translation: And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized tax-booth idiom; rendered telones as tax collector

greek_text: και καταλιπων απαντα αναστας ηκολουθησεν αυτω
transliteration: kai katalipwn apanta anastav hkolouyhsen autw
draft_translation: And he left all, rose up, and followed him.
ukjv_translation: And he left all, rose up, and followed him.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: και εποιησεν δοχην μεγαλην ο λευις αυτω εν τη οικια αυτου και ην οχλος τελωνων πολυς και αλλων οι ησαν μετ αυτων κατακειμενοι
transliteration: kai epoihsen dochn megalhn o leuiv autw en th oikia autou kai hn oclov telwnwn poluv kai allwn oi hsan met autwn katakeimenoi
draft_translation: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of tax collectors and of others that sat down with them.
ukjv_translation: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them.

greek_text: και εγογγυζον οι γραμματεις αυτων και οι φαρισαιοι προς τους μαθητας αυτου λεγοντες δια τι μετα τελωνων και αμαρτωλων εσθιετε και πινετε
transliteration: kai egogguzon oi grammateiv autwn kai oi farisaioi prov touv mayhtav autou legontev dia ti meta telwnwn kai amartwlwn esyiete kai pinete
draft_translation: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?
ukjv_translation: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do all of you eat and drink with publicans and sinners?
review_notes: removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact; rendered telones as tax collector

greek_text: και αποκριθεις ο ιησους ειπεν προς αυτους ου χρειαν εχουσιν οι υγιαινοντες ιατρου αλλ οι κακως εχοντες
transliteration: kai apokriyeiv o ihsouv eipen prov autouv ou creian ecousin oi ugiainontev iatrou all oi kakwv econtev
draft_translation: And Jesus answering said to them, Those who are well do not need a physician; but those who are sick.
ukjv_translation: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.

greek_text: ουκ εληλυθα καλεσαι δικαιους αλλα αμαρτωλους εις μετανοιαν
transliteration: ouk elhluya kalesai dikaiouv alla amartwlouv eiv metanoian
draft_translation: I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
ukjv_translation: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

greek_text: οι δε ειπον προς αυτον δια τι οι μαθηται ιωαννου νηστευουσιν πυκνα και δεησεις ποιουνται ομοιως και οι των φαρισαιων οι δε σοι εσθιουσιν και πινουσιν
transliteration: oi de eipon prov auton dia ti oi mayhtai iwannou nhsteuousin pukna kai dehseiv poiountai omoiwv kai oi twn farisaiwn oi de soi esyiousin kai pinousin
draft_translation: And they said to him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but yours eat and drink?
ukjv_translation: And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but yours eat and drink?

greek_text: ο δε ειπεν προς αυτους μη δυνασθε τους υιους του νυμφωνος εν ω ο νυμφιος μετ αυτων εστιν ποιησαι νηστευειν
transliteration: o de eipen prov autouv mh dunasye touv uiouv tou numfwnov en w o numfiov met autwn estin poihsai nhsteuein
draft_translation: And he said to them, Can you make the children of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
ukjv_translation: And he said unto them, Can all of you make the children of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?

greek_text: ελευσονται δε ημεραι και οταν απαρθη απ αυτων ο νυμφιος τοτε νηστευσουσιν εν εκειναις ταις ημεραις
transliteration: eleusontai de hmerai kai otan aparyh ap autwn o numfiov tote nhsteusousin en ekeinaiv taiv hmeraiv
draft_translation: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
ukjv_translation: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: ελεγεν δε και παραβολην προς αυτους οτι ουδεις επιβλημα ιματιου καινου επιβαλλει επι ιματιον παλαιον ει δε μηγε και το καινον σχιζει και τω παλαιω ου συμφωνει επιβλημα το απο του καινου
transliteration: elegen de kai parabolhn prov autouv oti oudeiv epiblhma imatiou kainou epiballei epi imation palaion ei de mhge kai to kainon scizei kai tw palaiw ou sumfwnei epiblhma to apo tou kainou
draft_translation: And he spoke also a parable to them; No one puts a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new makes a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agrees not with the old.
ukjv_translation: And he spoke also a parable unto them; No man puts a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new makes a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agrees not with the old.
review_notes: cleaned new-garment wording; modernized archaic directional unto; modernized garment where not contextually technical; modernized no-man idiom

greek_text: και ουδεις βαλλει οινον νεον εις ασκους παλαιους ει δε μηγε ρηξει ο νεος οινος τους ασκους και αυτος εκχυθησεται και οι ασκοι απολουνται
transliteration: kai oudeiv ballei oinon neon eiv askouv palaiouv ei de mhge rhxei o neov oinov touv askouv kai autov ekcuyhsetai kai oi askoi apolountai
draft_translation: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; else the new wine will burst the wineskins, and be spilled, and the wineskins shall perish.
ukjv_translation: And no man puts new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.
review_notes: modernized no-man idiom; rendered askos as wineskin

greek_text: αλλα οινον νεον εις ασκους καινους βλητεον και αμφοτεροι συντηρουνται
transliteration: alla oinon neon eiv askouv kainouv blhteon kai amfoteroi sunthrountai
draft_translation: But new wine must be put into new wineskins; and both are preserved.
ukjv_translation: But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.

greek_text: και ουδεις πιων παλαιον ευθεως θελει νεον λεγει γαρ ο παλαιος χρηστοτερος εστιν
transliteration: kai oudeiv piwn palaion euyewv yelei neon legei gar o palaiov crhstoterov estin
draft_translation: No one also having drunk old wine immediately desires new: for he says, The old is better.
ukjv_translation: No man also having drunk old wine immediately desires new: for he says, The old is better.

greek_text: εγενετο δε εν σαββατω δευτεροπρωτω διαπορευεσθαι αυτον δια των σποριμων και ετιλλον οι μαθηται αυτου τους σταχυας και ησθιον ψωχοντες ταις χερσιν
transliteration: egeneto de en sabbatw deuteroprwtw diaporeuesyai auton dia twn sporimwn kai etillon oi mayhtai autou touv stacuav kai hsyion qwcontev taiv cersin
draft_translation: And it happened on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the grain fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of grain, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.
review_notes: modernized came-to-pass idiom; modernized corn as grain

greek_text: τινες δε των φαρισαιων ειπον αυτοις τι ποιειτε ο ουκ εξεστιν ποιειν εν τοις σαββασιν
transliteration: tinev de twn farisaiwn eipon autoiv ti poieite o ouk exestin poiein en toiv sabbasin
draft_translation: And certain of the Pharisees said to them, Why do you do that which is not lawful to do on the Sabbath?
ukjv_translation: And certain of the Pharisees said unto them, Why do all of you that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?

greek_text: και αποκριθεις προς αυτους ειπεν ο ιησους ουδε τουτο ανεγνωτε ο εποιησεν δαβιδ οποτε επεινασεν αυτος και οι μετ αυτου οντες
transliteration: kai apokriyeiv prov autouv eipen o ihsouv oude touto anegnwte o epoihsen dabid opote epeinasen autov kai oi met autou ontev
draft_translation: And Jesus answering them said, Have you not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was hungry, and those who were with him;
ukjv_translation: And Jesus answering them said, Have all of you not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungered, and they which were with him;
review_notes: modernized an-hungered idiom; modernized they-which relative; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: ως εισηλθεν εις τον οικον του θεου και τους αρτους της προθεσεως ελαβεν και εφαγεν και εδωκεν και τοις μετ αυτου ους ουκ εξεστιν φαγειν ει μη μονους τους ιερεις
transliteration: wv eishlyen eiv ton oikon tou yeou kai touv artouv thv proyesewv elaben kai efagen kai edwken kai toiv met autou ouv ouk exestin fagein ei mh monouv touv iereiv
draft_translation: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the showbread, and gave also to those who were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?
ukjv_translation: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the showbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?

greek_text: και ελεγεν αυτοις οτι κυριος εστιν ο υιος του ανθρωπου και του σαββατου
transliteration: kai elegen autoiv oti kuriov estin o uiov tou anyrwpou kai tou sabbatou
draft_translation: And he said to them, The Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
ukjv_translation: And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

greek_text: εγενετο δε και εν ετερω σαββατω εισελθειν αυτον εις την συναγωγην και διδασκειν και ην εκει ανθρωπος και η χειρ αυτου η δεξια ην ξηρα
transliteration: egeneto de kai en eterw sabbatw eiselyein auton eiv thn sunagwghn kai didaskein kai hn ekei anyrwpov kai h ceir autou h dexia hn xhra
draft_translation: And it happened also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.

greek_text: παρετηρουν δε αυτον οι γραμματεις και οι φαρισαιοι ει εν τω σαββατω θεραπευσει ινα ευρωσιν κατηγοριαν αυτου
transliteration: parethroun de auton oi grammateiv kai oi farisaioi ei en tw sabbatw yerapeusei ina eurwsin kathgorian autou
draft_translation: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the Sabbath; that they might find an accusation against him.
ukjv_translation: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.

greek_text: αυτος δε ηδει τους διαλογισμους αυτων και ειπεν τω ανθρωπω τω ξηραν εχοντι την χειρα εγειραι και στηθι εις το μεσον ο δε αναστας εστη
transliteration: autov de hdei touv dialogismouv autwn kai eipen tw anyrwpw tw xhran econti thn ceira egeirai kai sthyi eiv to meson o de anastav esth
draft_translation: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man who had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.
ukjv_translation: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.

greek_text: ειπεν ουν ο ιησους προς αυτους επερωτησω υμας τι εξεστιν τοις σαββασιν αγαθοποιησαι η κακοποιησαι ψυχην σωσαι η απολεσαι
transliteration: eipen oun o ihsouv prov autouv eperwthsw umav ti exestin toiv sabbasin agayopoihsai h kakopoihsai quchn swsai h apolesai
draft_translation: Then Jesus said to them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do evil? To save life, or to destroy it?
ukjv_translation: Then said Jesus unto them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it?

greek_text: και περιβλεψαμενος παντας αυτους ειπεν τω ανθρωπω εκτεινον την χειρα σου ο δε εποιησεν ουτως και αποκατεσταθη η χειρ αυτου υγιης ως η αλλη
transliteration: kai peribleqamenov pantav autouv eipen tw anyrwpw ekteinon thn ceira sou o de epoihsen outwv kai apokatestayh h ceir autou ugihv wv h allh
draft_translation: And looking around upon them all, he said to the man, Stretch forth your hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
ukjv_translation: And looking round about upon them all, he said unto the man, Stretch forth your hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

greek_text: αυτοι δε επλησθησαν ανοιας και διελαλουν προς αλληλους τι αν ποιησειαν τω ιησου
transliteration: autoi de eplhsyhsan anoiav kai dielaloun prov allhlouv ti an poihseian tw ihsou
draft_translation: And they were filled with fury; and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus.
ukjv_translation: And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.

greek_text: εγενετο δε εν ταις ημεραις ταυταις εξηλθεν εις το ορος προσευξασθαι και ην διανυκτερευων εν τη προσευχη του θεου
transliteration: egeneto de en taiv hmeraiv tautaiv exhlyen eiv to orov proseuxasyai kai hn dianuktereuwn en th proseuch tou yeou
draft_translation: And it happened in those days, that he went out onto a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.

greek_text: και οτε εγενετο ημερα προσεφωνησεν τους μαθητας αυτου και εκλεξαμενος απ αυτων δωδεκα ους και αποστολους ωνομασεν
transliteration: kai ote egeneto hmera prosefwnhsen touv mayhtav autou kai eklexamenov ap autwn dwdeka ouv kai apostolouv wnomasen
draft_translation: And when it was day, he called to him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
ukjv_translation: And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;

greek_text: σιμωνα ον και ωνομασεν πετρον και ανδρεαν τον αδελφον αυτου ιακωβον και ιωαννην φιλιππον και βαρθολομαιον
transliteration: simwna on kai wnomasen petron kai andrean ton adelfon autou iakwbon kai iwannhn filippon kai baryolomaion
draft_translation: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
ukjv_translation: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: ματθαιον και θωμαν ιακωβον τον του αλφαιου και σιμωνα τον καλουμενον ζηλωτην
transliteration: matyaion kai ywman iakwbon ton tou alfaiou kai simwna ton kaloumenon zhlwthn
draft_translation: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called the Zealot,
ukjv_translation: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes,

greek_text: ιουδαν ιακωβου και ιουδαν ισκαριωτην ος και εγενετο προδοτης
transliteration: ioudan iakwbou kai ioudan iskariwthn ov kai egeneto prodothv
draft_translation: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.
ukjv_translation: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: και καταβας μετ αυτων εστη επι τοπου πεδινου και οχλος μαθητων αυτου και πληθος πολυ του λαου απο πασης της ιουδαιας και ιερουσαλημ και της παραλιου τυρου και σιδωνος οι ηλθον ακουσαι αυτου και ιαθηναι απο των νοσων αυτων
transliteration: kai katabav met autwn esth epi topou pedinou kai oclov mayhtwn autou kai plhyov polu tou laou apo pashv thv ioudaiav kai ierousalhm kai thv paraliou turou kai sidwnov oi hlyon akousai autou kai iayhnai apo twn noswn autwn
draft_translation: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great crowd of people out of all Judea and Jerusalem, and from the seashore of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
ukjv_translation: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judaea and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
review_notes: modernized sea-coast idiom; rendered ochlos as crowd; standardized Judea spelling

greek_text: και οι οχλουμενοι υπο πνευματων ακαθαρτων και εθεραπευοντο
transliteration: kai oi ocloumenoi upo pneumatwn akayartwn kai eyerapeuonto
draft_translation: And those who were troubled with unclean spirits: and they were healed.
ukjv_translation: And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: (o. pneuma) and they were healed.

greek_text: και πας ο οχλος εζητει απτεσθαι αυτου οτι δυναμις παρ αυτου εξηρχετο και ιατο παντας
transliteration: kai pav o oclov ezhtei aptesyai autou oti dunamiv par autou exhrceto kai iato pantav
draft_translation: And the whole crowd sought to touch him: for power went out of him, and healed them all.
ukjv_translation: And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.

greek_text: και αυτος επαρας τους οφθαλμους αυτου εις τους μαθητας αυτου ελεγεν μακαριοι οι πτωχοι οτι υμετερα εστιν η βασιλεια του θεου
transliteration: kai autov eparav touv ofyalmouv autou eiv touv mayhtav autou elegen makarioi oi ptwcoi oti umetera estin h basileia tou yeou
draft_translation: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed are you poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
ukjv_translation: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed be all of you poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
review_notes: fixed yours artifact; modernized blessed-be-you wording; modernized yours before noun; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: μακαριοι οι πεινωντες νυν οτι χορτασθησεσθε μακαριοι οι κλαιοντες νυν οτι γελασετε
transliteration: makarioi oi peinwntev nun oti cortasyhsesye makarioi oi klaiontev nun oti gelasete
draft_translation: Blessed are you that hunger now: for you shall be filled. Blessed are you that weep now: for you shall laugh.
ukjv_translation: Blessed are all of you that hunger now: for all of you shall be filled. Blessed are all of you that weep now: for all of you shall laugh.

greek_text: μακαριοι εστε οταν μισησωσιν υμας οι ανθρωποι και οταν αφορισωσιν υμας και ονειδισωσιν και εκβαλωσιν το ονομα υμων ως πονηρον ενεκα του υιου του ανθρωπου
transliteration: makarioi este otan mishswsin umav oi anyrwpoi kai otan aforiswsin umav kai oneidiswsin kai ekbalwsin to onoma umwn wv ponhron eneka tou uiou tou anyrwpou
draft_translation: Blessed are you, when people shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake.
ukjv_translation: Blessed are all of you, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake.

greek_text: χαιρετε εν εκεινη τη ημερα και σκιρτησατε ιδου γαρ ο μισθος υμων πολυς εν τω ουρανω κατα ταυτα γαρ εποιουν τοις προφηταις οι πατερες αυτων
transliteration: cairete en ekeinh th hmera kai skirthsate idou gar o misyov umwn poluv en tw ouranw kata tauta gar epoioun toiv profhtaiv oi paterev autwn
draft_translation: Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy: for, look, your reward is great in heaven: for in like manner did their fathers to the prophets.
ukjv_translation: Rejoice all of you in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

greek_text: πλην ουαι υμιν τοις πλουσιοις οτι απεχετε την παρακλησιν υμων
transliteration: plhn ouai umin toiv plousioiv oti apecete thn paraklhsin umwn
draft_translation: But woe to you that are rich! for you have received your consolation.
ukjv_translation: But woe unto you that are rich! for all of you have received your consolation.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: ουαι υμιν οι εμπεπλησμενοι οτι πεινασετε ουαι υμιν οι γελωντες νυν οτι πενθησετε και κλαυσετε
transliteration: ouai umin oi empeplhsmenoi oti peinasete ouai umin oi gelwntev nun oti penyhsete kai klausete
draft_translation: Woe to you that are full! for you shall hunger. Woe to you that laugh now! for you shall mourn and weep.
ukjv_translation: Woe unto you that are full! for all of you shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for all of you shall mourn and weep.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: ουαι υμιν οταν καλως υμας ειπωσιν παντες οι ανθρωποι κατα ταυτα γαρ εποιουν τοις ψευδοπροφηταις οι πατερες αυτων
transliteration: ouai umin otan kalwv umav eipwsin pantev oi anyrwpoi kata tauta gar epoioun toiv qeudoprofhtaiv oi paterev autwn
draft_translation: Woe to you, when all people shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
ukjv_translation: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

greek_text: αλλ υμιν λεγω τοις ακουουσιν αγαπατε τους εχθρους υμων καλως ποιειτε τοις μισουσιν υμας
transliteration: all umin legw toiv akouousin agapate touv ecyrouv umwn kalwv poieite toiv misousin umav
draft_translation: But I say to you who hear, Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
ukjv_translation: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,

greek_text: ευλογειτε τους καταρωμενους υμιν και προσευχεσθε υπερ των επηρεαζοντων υμας
transliteration: eulogeite touv katarwmenouv umin kai proseucesye uper twn ephreazontwn umav
draft_translation: Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who despitefully use you.
ukjv_translation: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.
review_notes: modernized them-that relative; modernized them-which relative

greek_text: τω τυπτοντι σε επι την σιαγονα παρεχε και την αλλην και απο του αιροντος σου το ιματιον και τον χιτωνα μη κωλυσης
transliteration: tw tuptonti se epi thn siagona parece kai thn allhn kai apo tou airontov sou to imation kai ton citwna mh kwlushv
draft_translation: And to him who strikes you on the one cheek offer also the other; and him who takes away your cloak forbid not to take your tunic also.
ukjv_translation: And unto him that strikes you on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that takes away your cloak forbid not to take your coat also.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized him-that relative; rendered chiton as tunic

greek_text: παντι δε τω αιτουντι σε διδου και απο του αιροντος τα σα μη απαιτει
transliteration: panti de tw aitounti se didou kai apo tou airontov ta sa mh apaitei
draft_translation: Give to everyone who asks of you; and of him who takes away your goods do not ask them back.
ukjv_translation: Give to every man that asks of you; and of him that takes away your goods ask them not again.

greek_text: και καθως θελετε ινα ποιωσιν υμιν οι ανθρωποι και υμεις ποιειτε αυτοις ομοιως
transliteration: kai kaywv yelete ina poiwsin umin oi anyrwpoi kai umeiv poieite autoiv omoiwv
draft_translation: And as you would that men should do to you, do you also to them likewise.
ukjv_translation: And as all of you would that men should do to you, do all of you also to them likewise.

greek_text: και ει αγαπατε τους αγαπωντας υμας ποια υμιν χαρις εστιν και γαρ οι αμαρτωλοι τους αγαπωντας αυτους αγαπωσιν
transliteration: kai ei agapate touv agapwntav umav poia umin cariv estin kai gar oi amartwloi touv agapwntav autouv agapwsin
draft_translation: For if you love those who love you, what credit have you? for sinners also love those who love them.
ukjv_translation: For if all of you love them which love you, what thank have all of you? for sinners also love those that love them.

greek_text: και εαν αγαθοποιητε τους αγαθοποιουντας υμας ποια υμιν χαρις εστιν και γαρ οι αμαρτωλοι το αυτο ποιουσιν
transliteration: kai ean agayopoihte touv agayopoiountav umav poia umin cariv estin kai gar oi amartwloi to auto poiousin
draft_translation: And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit have you? for sinners also do the same.
ukjv_translation: And if all of you do good to them which do good to you, what thank have all of you? for sinners also do even the same.

greek_text: και εαν δανειζητε παρ ων ελπιζητε απολαβειν ποια υμιν χαρις εστιν και γαρ οι αμαρτωλοι αμαρτωλοις δανειζουσιν ινα απολαβωσιν τα ισα
transliteration: kai ean daneizhte par wn elpizhte apolabein poia umin cariv estin kai gar oi amartwloi amartwloiv daneizousin ina apolabwsin ta isa
draft_translation: And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit have you? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.
ukjv_translation: And if all of you lend to them of whom all of you hope to receive, what thank have all of you? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

greek_text: πλην αγαπατε τους εχθρους υμων και αγαθοποιειτε και δανειζετε μηδεν απελπιζοντες και εσται ο μισθος υμων πολυς και εσεσθε υιοι του υψιστου οτι αυτος χρηστος εστιν επι τους αχαριστους και πονηρους
transliteration: plhn agapate touv ecyrouv umwn kai agayopoieite kai daneizete mhden apelpizontev kai estai o misyov umwn poluv kai esesye uioi tou uqistou oti autov crhstov estin epi touv acaristouv kai ponhrouv
draft_translation: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and you shall be the children of the Most High: for he is kind to the unthankful and to the evil.
ukjv_translation: But love all of you your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and all of you shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.

greek_text: γινεσθε ουν οικτιρμονες καθως και ο πατηρ υμων οικτιρμων εστιν
transliteration: ginesye oun oiktirmonev kaywv kai o pathr umwn oiktirmwn estin
draft_translation: Be therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
ukjv_translation: Be all of you therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
review_notes: modernized be-you imperative; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: μη κρινετε και ου μη κριθητε μη καταδικαζετε και ου μη καταδικασθητε απολυετε και απολυθησεσθε
transliteration: mh krinete kai ou mh kriyhte mh katadikazete kai ou mh katadikasyhte apoluete kai apoluyhsesye
draft_translation: Do not judge, and you shall not be judged: do not condemn, and you shall not be condemned: forgive, and you shall be forgiven:
ukjv_translation: Judge not, and all of you shall not be judged: condemn not, and all of you shall not be condemned: forgive, and all of you shall be forgiven:
review_notes: fixed sentence casing; modernized condemn-not idiom; modernized judge-not idiom; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: διδοτε και δοθησεται υμιν μετρον καλον πεπιεσμενον και σεσαλευμενον και υπερεκχυνομενον δωσουσιν εις τον κολπον υμων τω γαρ αυτω μετρω ω μετρειτε αντιμετρηθησεται υμιν
transliteration: didote kai doyhsetai umin metron kalon pepiesmenon kai sesaleumenon kai uperekcunomenon dwsousin eiv ton kolpon umwn tw gar autw metrw w metreite antimetrhyhsetai umin
draft_translation: Give, and it shall be given to you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall they give into your bosom. For with the same measure that you measure, it shall be measured to you again.
ukjv_translation: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that all of you mete likewise it shall be measured to you again.

greek_text: ειπεν δε παραβολην αυτοις μητι δυναται τυφλος τυφλον οδηγειν ουχι αμφοτεροι εις βοθυνον πεσουνται
transliteration: eipen de parabolhn autoiv mhti dunatai tuflov tuflon odhgein ouci amfoteroi eiv boyunon pesountai
draft_translation: And he spoke a parable to them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the pit?
ukjv_translation: And he spoke a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?

greek_text: ουκ εστιν μαθητης υπερ τον διδασκαλον αυτου κατηρτισμενος δε πας εσται ως ο διδασκαλος αυτου
transliteration: ouk estin mayhthv uper ton didaskalon autou kathrtismenov de pav estai wv o didaskalov autou
draft_translation: The disciple is not above his teacher: but every one who is perfected shall be as his teacher.
ukjv_translation: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.

greek_text: τι δε βλεπεις το καρφος το εν τω οφθαλμω του αδελφου σου την δε δοκον την εν τω ιδιω οφθαλμω ου κατανοεις
transliteration: ti de blepeiv to karfov to en tw ofyalmw tou adelfou sou thn de dokon thn en tw idiw ofyalmw ou katanoeiv
draft_translation: And why do you look at the splinter that is in your brother's eye, but do not perceive the beam that is in your own eye?
ukjv_translation: And why behold you the splinter that is in your brother's eye, but perceive not the beam that is in yours own eye?

greek_text: η πως δυνασαι λεγειν τω αδελφω σου αδελφε αφες εκβαλω το καρφος το εν τω οφθαλμω σου αυτος την εν τω οφθαλμω σου δοκον ου βλεπων υποκριτα εκβαλε πρωτον την δοκον εκ του οφθαλμου σου και τοτε διαβλεψεις εκβαλειν το καρφος το εν τω οφθαλμω του αδελφου σου
transliteration: h pwv dunasai legein tw adelfw sou adelfe afev ekbalw to karfov to en tw ofyalmw sou autov thn en tw ofyalmw sou dokon ou blepwn upokrita ekbale prwton thn dokon ek tou ofyalmou sou kai tote diableqeiv ekbalein to karfov to en tw ofyalmw tou adelfou sou
draft_translation: Or how can you say to your brother, Brother, let me pull out the splinter that is in your eye, when you yourself do not see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of your own eye, and then shall you see clearly to pull out the splinter that is in your brother's eye.
ukjv_translation: Either how can you say to your brother, Brother, let me pull out the splinter that is in yours eye, when you yourself behold not the beam that is in yours own eye? You hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of yours own eye, and then shall you see clearly to pull out the splinter that is in your brother's eye.

greek_text: ου γαρ εστιν δενδρον καλον ποιουν καρπον σαπρον ουδε δενδρον σαπρον ποιουν καρπον καλον
transliteration: ou gar estin dendron kalon poioun karpon sapron oude dendron sapron poioun karpon kalon
draft_translation: For a good tree does not bring forth corrupt fruit; neither does a corrupt tree bear good fruit.
ukjv_translation: For a good tree brings not forth corrupt fruit; neither does a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
review_notes: modernized brings-not wording; modernized childbirth bring-forth idiom

greek_text: εκαστον γαρ δενδρον εκ του ιδιου καρπου γινωσκεται ου γαρ εξ ακανθων συλλεγουσιν συκα ουδε εκ βατου τρυγωσιν σταφυλην
transliteration: ekaston gar dendron ek tou idiou karpou ginwsketai ou gar ex akanywn sullegousin suka oude ek batou trugwsin stafulhn
draft_translation: For every tree is known by its own fruit. For from thorns people do not gather figs, nor from a bramble bush do they gather grapes.
ukjv_translation: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

greek_text: ο αγαθος ανθρωπος εκ του αγαθου θησαυρου της καρδιας αυτου προφερει το αγαθον και ο πονηρος ανθρωπος εκ του πονηρου θησαυρου της καρδιας αυτου προφερει το πονηρον εκ γαρ του περισσευματος της καρδιας λαλει το στομα αυτου
transliteration: o agayov anyrwpov ek tou agayou yhsaurou thv kardiav autou proferei to agayon kai o ponhrov anyrwpov ek tou ponhrou yhsaurou thv kardiav autou proferei to ponhron ek gar tou perisseumatov thv kardiav lalei to stoma autou
draft_translation: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart produces that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart produces that which is evil: for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks.
ukjv_translation: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks.

greek_text: τι δε με καλειτε κυριε κυριε και ου ποιειτε α λεγω
transliteration: ti de me kaleite kurie kurie kai ou poieite a legw
draft_translation: And why do you call me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
ukjv_translation: And why call all of you me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

greek_text: πας ο ερχομενος προς με και ακουων μου των λογων και ποιων αυτους υποδειξω υμιν τινι εστιν ομοιος
transliteration: pav o ercomenov prov me kai akouwn mou twn logwn kai poiwn autouv upodeixw umin tini estin omoiov
draft_translation: Whoever comes to me, and hears my sayings, and does them, I will show you to whom he is like:
ukjv_translation: Whosoever comes to me, and hears my sayings, (o. logos) and does them, I will show you to whom he is like:
review_notes: modernized whosoever; removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker

greek_text: ομοιος εστιν ανθρωπω οικοδομουντι οικιαν ος εσκαψεν και εβαθυνεν και εθηκεν θεμελιον επι την πετραν πλημμυρας δε γενομενης προσερρηξεν ο ποταμος τη οικια εκεινη και ουκ ισχυσεν σαλευσαι αυτην τεθεμελιωτο γαρ επι την πετραν
transliteration: omoiov estin anyrwpw oikodomounti oikian ov eskaqen kai ebayunen kai eyhken yemelion epi thn petran plhmmurav de genomenhv proserrhxen o potamov th oikia ekeinh kai ouk iscusen saleusai authn teyemeliwto gar epi thn petran
draft_translation: He is like a man who built a house, and dug deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat violently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.
ukjv_translation: He is like a man which built an house, and dug deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

greek_text: ο δε ακουσας και μη ποιησας ομοιος εστιν ανθρωπω οικοδομησαντι οικιαν επι την γην χωρις θεμελιου η προσερρηξεν ο ποταμος και ευθεως επεσεν και εγενετο το ρηγμα της οικιας εκεινης μεγα
transliteration: o de akousav kai mh poihsav omoiov estin anyrwpw oikodomhsanti oikian epi thn ghn cwriv yemeliou h proserrhxen o potamov kai euyewv epesen kai egeneto to rhgma thv oikiav ekeinhv mega
draft_translation: But the one who hears, and does not, is like a man that without a foundation built a house upon the earth; against which the stream beat violently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.
ukjv_translation: But he that hears, and does not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.

greek_text: επει δε επληρωσεν παντα τα ρηματα αυτου εις τας ακοας του λαου εισηλθεν εις καπερναουμ
transliteration: epei de eplhrwsen panta ta rhmata autou eiv tav akoav tou laou eishlyen eiv kapernaoum
draft_translation: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
ukjv_translation: Now when he had ended all his sayings (o. rhema) in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

greek_text: εκατονταρχου δε τινος δουλος κακως εχων ημελλεν τελευταν ος ην αυτω εντιμος
transliteration: ekatontarcou de tinov doulov kakwv ecwn hmellen teleutan ov hn autw entimov
draft_translation: And a certain centurion's slave, who was dear to him, was sick, and ready to die.
ukjv_translation: And a certain centurion's servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; rendered doulos-family wording as slave

greek_text: ακουσας δε περι του ιησου απεστειλεν προς αυτον πρεσβυτερους των ιουδαιων ερωτων αυτον οπως ελθων διασωση τον δουλον αυτου
transliteration: akousav de peri tou ihsou apesteilen prov auton presbuterouv twn ioudaiwn erwtwn auton opwv elywn diaswsh ton doulon autou
draft_translation: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent to him the elders of the Jews, begging him who he would come and heal his slave.
ukjv_translation: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized beseeching; modernized him-that relative; rendered doulos-family wording as slave

greek_text: οι δε παραγενομενοι προς τον ιησουν παρεκαλουν αυτον σπουδαιως λεγοντες οτι αξιος εστιν ω παρεξει τουτο
transliteration: oi de paragenomenoi prov ton ihsoun parekaloun auton spoudaiwv legontev oti axiov estin w parexei touto
draft_translation: And when they came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
ukjv_translation: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:

greek_text: αγαπα γαρ το εθνος ημων και την συναγωγην αυτος ωκοδομησεν ημιν
transliteration: agapa gar to eynov hmwn kai thn sunagwghn autov wkodomhsen hmin
draft_translation: For he loves our nation, and he has built us a synagogue.
ukjv_translation: For he loves our nation, and he has built us a synagogue.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: ο δε ιησους επορευετο συν αυτοις ηδη δε αυτου ου μακραν απεχοντος απο της οικιας επεμψεν προς αυτον ο εκατονταρχος φιλους λεγων αυτω κυριε μη σκυλλου ου γαρ ειμι ικανος ινα υπο την στεγην μου εισελθης
transliteration: o de ihsouv eporeueto sun autoiv hdh de autou ou makran apecontov apo thv oikiav epemqen prov auton o ekatontarcov filouv legwn autw kurie mh skullou ou gar eimi ikanov ina upo thn steghn mou eiselyhv
draft_translation: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, Lord, do not trouble yourself: for I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof:
ukjv_translation: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not yourself: for I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof:

greek_text: διο ουδε εμαυτον ηξιωσα προς σε ελθειν αλλα ειπε λογω και ιαθησεται ο παις μου
transliteration: dio oude emauton hxiwsa prov se elyein alla eipe logw kai iayhsetai o paiv mou
draft_translation: Therefore neither did I think myself worthy to come to you: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.
ukjv_translation: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto you: but say in a word, (o. logos) and my servant shall be healed.

greek_text: και γαρ εγω ανθρωπος ειμι υπο εξουσιαν τασσομενος εχων υπ εμαυτον στρατιωτας και λεγω τουτω πορευθητι και πορευεται και αλλω ερχου και ερχεται και τω δουλω μου ποιησον τουτο και ποιει
transliteration: kai gar egw anyrwpov eimi upo exousian tassomenov ecwn up emauton stratiwtav kai legw toutw poreuyhti kai poreuetai kai allw ercou kai ercetai kai tw doulw mou poihson touto kai poiei
draft_translation: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say to one, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my slave, Do this, and he does it.
ukjv_translation: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; rendered doulos-family wording as slave

greek_text: ακουσας δε ταυτα ο ιησους εθαυμασεν αυτον και στραφεις τω ακολουθουντι αυτω οχλω ειπεν λεγω υμιν ουδε εν τω ισραηλ τοσαυτην πιστιν ευρον
transliteration: akousav de tauta o ihsouv eyaumasen auton kai strafeiv tw akolouyounti autw oclw eipen legw umin oude en tw israhl tosauthn pistin euron
draft_translation: When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned him about, and said to the people that followed him, I say to you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
ukjv_translation: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized marvelled spelling

greek_text: και υποστρεψαντες οι πεμφθεντες εις τον οικον ευρον τον ασθενουντα δουλον υγιαινοντα
transliteration: kai upostreqantev oi pemfyentev eiv ton oikon euron ton asyenounta doulon ugiainonta
draft_translation: And those who were sent, returning to the house, found the slave whole that had been sick.
ukjv_translation: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.
review_notes: modernized they-that relative; rendered doulos-family wording as slave

greek_text: και εγενετο εν τη εξης επορευετο εις πολιν καλουμενην ναιν και συνεπορευοντο αυτω οι μαθηται αυτου ικανοι και οχλος πολυς
transliteration: kai egeneto en th exhv eporeueto eiv polin kaloumenhn nain kai suneporeuonto autw oi mayhtai autou ikanoi kai oclov poluv
draft_translation: And it happened the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and a great crowd.
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.

greek_text: ως δε ηγγισεν τη πυλη της πολεως και ιδου εξεκομιζετο τεθνηκως υιος μονογενης τη μητρι αυτου και αυτη ην χηρα και οχλος της πολεως ικανος ην συν αυτη
transliteration: wv de hggisen th pulh thv polewv kai idou exekomizeto teynhkwv uiov monogenhv th mhtri autou kai auth hn chra kai oclov thv polewv ikanov hn sun auth
draft_translation: Now when he came near to the gate of the city, look, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and a great crowd of the city was with her.
ukjv_translation: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.

greek_text: και ιδων αυτην ο κυριος εσπλαγχνισθη επ αυτη και ειπεν αυτη μη κλαιε
transliteration: kai idwn authn o kuriov esplagcnisyh ep auth kai eipen auth mh klaie
draft_translation: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said to her, Do not weep.
ukjv_translation: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

greek_text: και προσελθων ηψατο της σορου οι δε βασταζοντες εστησαν και ειπεν νεανισκε σοι λεγω εγερθητι
transliteration: kai proselywn hqato thv sorou oi de bastazontev esthsan kai eipen neaniske soi legw egeryhti
draft_translation: And he came and touched the bier: and those who bore him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say to you, Rise.
ukjv_translation: And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto you, Arise.

greek_text: και ανεκαθισεν ο νεκρος και ηρξατο λαλειν και εδωκεν αυτον τη μητρι αυτου
transliteration: kai anekayisen o nekrov kai hrxato lalein kai edwken auton th mhtri autou
draft_translation: And the one who was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
ukjv_translation: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.

greek_text: ελαβεν δε φοβος απαντας και εδοξαζον τον θεον λεγοντες οτι προφητης μεγας εγηγερται εν ημιν και οτι επεσκεψατο ο θεος τον λαον αυτου
transliteration: elaben de fobov apantav kai edoxazon ton yeon legontev oti profhthv megav eghgertai en hmin kai oti epeskeqato o yeov ton laon autou
draft_translation: And fear came on all: and they glorified God, saying, A great prophet has risen up among us; and, God has visited his people.
ukjv_translation: And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet has risen up among us; and, That God has visited his people.

greek_text: και εξηλθεν ο λογος ουτος εν ολη τη ιουδαια περι αυτου και εν παση τη περιχωρω
transliteration: kai exhlyen o logov outov en olh th ioudaia peri autou kai en pash th pericwrw
draft_translation: And this report of him went forth throughout all Judea, and throughout all the region around.
ukjv_translation: And this rumour (o. logos) of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about.

greek_text: και απηγγειλαν ιωαννη οι μαθηται αυτου περι παντων τουτων
transliteration: kai aphggeilan iwannh oi mayhtai autou peri pantwn toutwn
draft_translation: And the disciples of John told him about all these things.
ukjv_translation: And the disciples of John showed him of all these things.

greek_text: και προσκαλεσαμενος δυο τινας των μαθητων αυτου ο ιωαννης επεμψεν προς τον ιησουν λεγων συ ει ο ερχομενος η αλλον προσδοκωμεν
transliteration: kai proskalesamenov duo tinav twn mayhtwn autou o iwannhv epemqen prov ton ihsoun legwn su ei o ercomenov h allon prosdokwmen
draft_translation: And John calling to him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Are you the one who should come? or should we look for another?
ukjv_translation: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Are you he that should come? or look we for another?

greek_text: παραγενομενοι δε προς αυτον οι ανδρες ειπον ιωαννης ο βαπτιστης απεσταλκεν ημας προς σε λεγων συ ει ο ερχομενος η αλλον προσδοκωμεν
transliteration: paragenomenoi de prov auton oi andrev eipon iwannhv o baptisthv apestalken hmav prov se legwn su ei o ercomenov h allon prosdokwmen
draft_translation: When the men had come to him, they said, John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying, Are you the one who should come? or should we look for another?
ukjv_translation: When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist has sent us unto you, saying, Are you he that should come? or look we for another?

greek_text: εν αυτη δε τη ωρα εθεραπευσεν πολλους απο νοσων και μαστιγων και πνευματων πονηρων και τυφλοις πολλοις εχαρισατο το βλεπειν
transliteration: en auth de th wra eyerapeusen pollouv apo noswn kai mastigwn kai pneumatwn ponhrwn kai tufloiv polloiv ecarisato to blepein
draft_translation: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and to many that were blind he gave sight.
ukjv_translation: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; (o. pneuma) and unto many that were blind he gave sight.

greek_text: και αποκριθεις ο ιησους ειπεν αυτοις πορευθεντες απαγγειλατε ιωαννη α ειδετε και ηκουσατε οτι τυφλοι αναβλεπουσιν χωλοι περιπατουσιν λεπροι καθαριζονται κωφοι ακουουσιν νεκροι εγειρονται πτωχοι ευαγγελιζονται
transliteration: kai apokriyeiv o ihsouv eipen autoiv poreuyentev apaggeilate iwannh a eidete kai hkousate oti tufloi anablepousin cwloi peripatousin leproi kayarizontai kwfoi akouousin nekroi egeirontai ptwcoi euaggelizontai
draft_translation: Then Jesus answering said to them, Go your way, and tell John what things you have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the good news is preached.
ukjv_translation: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things all of you have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact; rendered euangelion as good news

greek_text: και μακαριος εστιν ος εαν μη σκανδαλισθη εν εμοι
transliteration: kai makariov estin ov ean mh skandalisyh en emoi
draft_translation: And blessed is he, whoever shall not be stumbled in me.
ukjv_translation: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
review_notes: modernized whosoever; rendered skandalizo as stumble

greek_text: απελθοντων δε των αγγελων ιωαννου ηρξατο λεγειν προς τους οχλους περι ιωαννου τι εξεληλυθατε εις την ερημον θεασασθαι καλαμον υπο ανεμου σαλευομενον
transliteration: apelyontwn de twn aggelwn iwannou hrxato legein prov touv oclouv peri iwannou ti exelhluyate eiv thn erhmon yeasasyai kalamon upo anemou saleuomenon
draft_translation: And when the messengers of John had departed, he began to speak to the people concerning John, What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
ukjv_translation: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went all of you out into the wilderness in order to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

greek_text: αλλα τι εξεληλυθατε ιδειν ανθρωπον εν μαλακοις ιματιοις ημφιεσμενον ιδου οι εν ιματισμω ενδοξω και τρυφη υπαρχοντες εν τοις βασιλειοις εισιν
transliteration: alla ti exelhluyate idein anyrwpon en malakoiv imatioiv hmfiesmenon idou oi en imatismw endoxw kai trufh uparcontev en toiv basileioiv eisin
draft_translation: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Look, those who are splendidly clothed, and live delicately, are in kings' courts.
ukjv_translation: But what went all of you out in order to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings' courts.

greek_text: αλλα τι εξεληλυθατε ιδειν προφητην ναι λεγω υμιν και περισσοτερον προφητου
transliteration: alla ti exelhluyate idein profhthn nai legw umin kai perissoteron profhtou
draft_translation: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and much more than a prophet.
ukjv_translation: But what went all of you out in order to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

greek_text: ουτος εστιν περι ου γεγραπται ιδου εγω αποστελλω τον αγγελον μου προ προσωπου σου ος κατασκευασει την οδον σου εμπροσθεν σου
transliteration: outov estin peri ou gegraptai idou egw apostellw ton aggelon mou pro proswpou sou ov kataskeuasei thn odon sou emprosyen sou
draft_translation: This is he, of whom it is written, Look, I send my messenger before your face, who shall prepare your way before you.
ukjv_translation: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before your face, which shall prepare your way before you.

greek_text: λεγω γαρ υμιν μειζων εν γεννητοις γυναικων προφητης ιωαννου του βαπτιστου ουδεις εστιν ο δε μικροτερος εν τη βασιλεια του θεου μειζων αυτου εστιν
transliteration: legw gar umin meizwn en gennhtoiv gunaikwn profhthv iwannou tou baptistou oudeiv estin o de mikroterov en th basileia tou yeou meizwn autou estin
draft_translation: For I say to you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
ukjv_translation: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

greek_text: και πας ο λαος ακουσας και οι τελωναι εδικαιωσαν τον θεον βαπτισθεντες το βαπτισμα ιωαννου
transliteration: kai pav o laov akousav kai oi telwnai edikaiwsan ton yeon baptisyentev to baptisma iwannou
draft_translation: And all the people that heard him, and the tax collectors, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
ukjv_translation: And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.

greek_text: οι δε φαρισαιοι και οι νομικοι την βουλην του θεου ηθετησαν εις εαυτους μη βαπτισθεντες υπ αυτου
transliteration: oi de farisaioi kai oi nomikoi thn boulhn tou yeou hyethsan eiv eautouv mh baptisyentev up autou
draft_translation: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God for themselves, not being baptized by him.
ukjv_translation: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.

greek_text: ειπεν δε ο κυριος τινι ουν ομοιωσω τους ανθρωπους της γενεας ταυτης και τινι εισιν ομοιοι
transliteration: eipen de o kuriov tini oun omoiwsw touv anyrwpouv thv geneav tauthv kai tini eisin omoioi
draft_translation: And the Lord said, To what then shall I liken the people of this generation? and to what are they like?
ukjv_translation: And the Lord said, Unto which then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?

greek_text: ομοιοι εισιν παιδιοις τοις εν αγορα καθημενοις και προσφωνουσιν αλληλοις και λεγουσιν ηυλησαμεν υμιν και ουκ ωρχησασθε εθρηνησαμεν υμιν και ουκ εκλαυσατε
transliteration: omoioi eisin paidioiv toiv en agora kayhmenoiv kai prosfwnousin allhloiv kai legousin hulhsamen umin kai ouk wrchsasye eyrhnhsamen umin kai ouk eklausate
draft_translation: They are like children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped to you, and you have not danced; we have mourned to you, and you have not wept.
ukjv_translation: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and all of you have not danced; we have mourned to you, and all of you have not wept.

greek_text: εληλυθεν γαρ ιωαννης ο βαπτιστης μητε αρτον εσθιων μητε οινον πινων και λεγετε δαιμονιον εχει
transliteration: elhluyen gar iwannhv o baptisthv mhte arton esyiwn mhte oinon pinwn kai legete daimonion ecei
draft_translation: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and you say, He has a demon.
ukjv_translation: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and all of you say, He has a devil.
review_notes: removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact; rendered daimonion as demon

greek_text: εληλυθεν ο υιος του ανθρωπου εσθιων και πινων και λεγετε ιδου ανθρωπος φαγος και οινοποτης τελωνων φιλος και αμαρτωλων
transliteration: elhluyen o uiov tou anyrwpou esyiwn kai pinwn kai legete idou anyrwpov fagov kai oinopothv telwnwn filov kai amartwlwn
draft_translation: The Son of man has come eating and drinking; and you say, Look a gluttonous man, and a wine indulger, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!
ukjv_translation: The Son of man has come eating and drinking; and all of you say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a wine indulger, a friend of publicans and sinners!
review_notes: modernized behold; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact; rendered telones as tax collector

greek_text: και εδικαιωθη η σοφια απο των τεκνων αυτης παντων
transliteration: kai edikaiwyh h sofia apo twn teknwn authv pantwn
draft_translation: But wisdom is justified by all her children.
ukjv_translation: But wisdom is justified of all her children.

greek_text: ηρωτα δε τις αυτον των φαρισαιων ινα φαγη μετ αυτου και εισελθων εις την οικιαν του φαρισαιου ανεκλιθη
transliteration: hrwta de tiv auton twn farisaiwn ina fagh met autou kai eiselywn eiv thn oikian tou farisaiou anekliyh
draft_translation: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee's house, and reclined at table.
ukjv_translation: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee's house, and sat down to food.
review_notes: fixed him-that relative artifact; modernized him-that relative; modernized reclining-at-meal idiom

greek_text: και ιδου γυνη εν τη πολει ητις ην αμαρτωλος επιγνουσα οτι ανακειται εν τη οικια του φαρισαιου κομισασα αλαβαστρον μυρου
transliteration: kai idou gunh en th polei htiv hn amartwlov epignousa oti anakeitai en th oikia tou farisaiou komisasa alabastron murou
draft_translation: And, look, a woman in the city, who was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus reclined at table in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,
ukjv_translation: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at food in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,

greek_text: και στασα παρα τους ποδας αυτου οπισω κλαιουσα ηρξατο βρεχειν τους ποδας αυτου τοις δακρυσιν και ταις θριξιν της κεφαλης αυτης εξεμασσεν και κατεφιλει τους ποδας αυτου και ηλειφεν τω μυρω
transliteration: kai stasa para touv podav autou opisw klaiousa hrxato brecein touv podav autou toiv dakrusin kai taiv yrixin thv kefalhv authv exemassen kai katefilei touv podav autou kai hleifen tw murw
draft_translation: And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
ukjv_translation: And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

greek_text: ιδων δε ο φαρισαιος ο καλεσας αυτον ειπεν εν εαυτω λεγων ουτος ει ην προφητης εγινωσκεν αν τις και ποταπη η γυνη ητις απτεται αυτου οτι αμαρτωλος εστιν
transliteration: idwn de o farisaiov o kalesav auton eipen en eautw legwn outov ei hn profhthv eginwsken an tiv kai potaph h gunh htiv aptetai autou oti amartwlov estin
draft_translation: Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw it, he spoke within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that touches him: for she is a sinner.
ukjv_translation: Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spoke within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that touches him: for she is a sinner.

greek_text: και αποκριθεις ο ιησους ειπεν προς αυτον σιμων εχω σοι τι ειπειν ο δε φησιν διδασκαλε ειπε
transliteration: kai apokriyeiv o ihsouv eipen prov auton simwn ecw soi ti eipein o de fhsin didaskale eipe
draft_translation: And Jesus answering said to him, Simon, I have something to say to you. And he says, Teacher, say it.
ukjv_translation: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto you. And he says, Master, say on.

greek_text: δυο χρεωφειλεται ησαν δανειστη τινι ο εις ωφειλεν δηναρια πεντακοσια ο δε ετερος πεντηκοντα
transliteration: duo crewfeiletai hsan daneisth tini o eiv wfeilen dhnaria pentakosia o de eterov penthkonta
draft_translation: There was a certain creditor who had two debtors: the one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
ukjv_translation: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.

greek_text: μη εχοντων δε αυτων αποδουναι αμφοτεροις εχαρισατο τις ουν αυτων ειπε πλειον αυτον αγαπησει
transliteration: mh econtwn de autwn apodounai amfoteroiv ecarisato tiv oun autwn eipe pleion auton agaphsei
draft_translation: And when they had nothing to pay, he freely forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?
ukjv_translation: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?

greek_text: αποκριθεις δε ο σιμων ειπεν υπολαμβανω οτι ω το πλειον εχαρισατο ο δε ειπεν αυτω ορθως εκρινας
transliteration: apokriyeiv de o simwn eipen upolambanw oti w to pleion ecarisato o de eipen autw orywv ekrinav
draft_translation: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said to him, You have rightly judged.
ukjv_translation: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, You have rightly judged.

greek_text: και στραφεις προς την γυναικα τω σιμωνι εφη βλεπεις ταυτην την γυναικα εισηλθον σου εις την οικιαν υδωρ επι τους ποδας μου ουκ εδωκας αυτη δε τοις δακρυσιν εβρεξεν μου τους ποδας και ταις θριξιν της κεφαλης αυτης εξεμαξεν
transliteration: kai strafeiv prov thn gunaika tw simwni efh blepeiv tauthn thn gunaika eishlyon sou eiv thn oikian udwr epi touv podav mou ouk edwkav auth de toiv dakrusin ebrexen mou touv podav kai taiv yrixin thv kefalhv authv exemaxen
draft_translation: And he turned to the woman, and said to Simon, Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, you gave me no water for my feet: but she has washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.
ukjv_translation: And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, See you this woman? I entered into yours house, you gave me no water for my feet: but she has washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.

greek_text: φιλημα μοι ουκ εδωκας αυτη δε αφ ης εισηλθον ου διελιπεν καταφιλουσα μου τους ποδας
transliteration: filhma moi ouk edwkav auth de af hv eishlyon ou dielipen katafilousa mou touv podav
draft_translation: You gave me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in has not ceased to kiss my feet.
ukjv_translation: You gave me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in has not ceased to kiss my feet.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: ελαιω την κεφαλην μου ουκ ηλειψας αυτη δε μυρω ηλειψεν μου τους ποδας
transliteration: elaiw thn kefalhn mou ouk hleiqav auth de murw hleiqen mou touv podav
draft_translation: My head with oil you did not anoint: but this woman has anointed my feet with ointment.
ukjv_translation: My head with oil you did not anoint: but this woman has anointed my feet with ointment.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: ου χαριν λεγω σοι αφεωνται αι αμαρτιαι αυτης αι πολλαι οτι ηγαπησεν πολυ ω δε ολιγον αφιεται ολιγον αγαπα
transliteration: ou carin legw soi afewntai ai amartiai authv ai pollai oti hgaphsen polu w de oligon afietai oligon agapa
draft_translation: Therefore I say to you, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.
ukjv_translation: Wherefore I say unto you, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized wherefore

greek_text: ειπεν δε αυτη αφεωνται σου αι αμαρτιαι
transliteration: eipen de auth afewntai sou ai amartiai
draft_translation: And he said to her, Your sins are forgiven.
ukjv_translation: And he said unto her, Your sins are forgiven.

greek_text: και ηρξαντο οι συνανακειμενοι λεγειν εν εαυτοις τις ουτος εστιν ος και αμαρτιας αφιησιν
transliteration: kai hrxanto oi sunanakeimenoi legein en eautoiv tiv outov estin ov kai amartiav afihsin
