draft_translation: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
ukjv_translation: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, (o. logos) he came into Greece,

greek_text: ποιησας τε μηνας τρεις γενομενης αυτω επιβουλης υπο των ιουδαιων μελλοντι αναγεσθαι εις την συριαν εγενετο γνωμη του υποστρεφειν δια μακεδονιας
transliteration: poihsav te mhnav treiv genomenhv autw epiboulhv upo twn ioudaiwn mellonti anagesyai eiv thn surian egeneto gnwmh tou upostrefein dia makedoniav
draft_translation: And there remained three months. And when a plot was made against him by the Jews, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
ukjv_translation: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.

greek_text: συνειπετο δε αυτω αχρι της ασιας σωπατρος βεροιαιος θεσσαλονικεων δε αρισταρχος και σεκουνδος και γαιος δερβαιος και τιμοθεος ασιανοι δε τυχικος και τροφιμος
transliteration: suneipeto de autw acri thv asiav swpatrov beroiaiov yessalonikewn de aristarcov kai sekoundov kai gaiov derbaiov kai timoyeov asianoi de tucikov kai trofimov
draft_translation: And there accompanied him as far as Asia Sopater the Berean; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
ukjv_translation: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.

greek_text: ουτοι προελθοντες εμενον ημας εν τρωαδι
transliteration: outoi proelyontev emenon hmav en trwadi
draft_translation: These going before waited for us at Troas.
ukjv_translation: These going before tarried for us at Troas.

greek_text: ημεις δε εξεπλευσαμεν μετα τας ημερας των αζυμων απο φιλιππων και ηλθομεν προς αυτους εις την τρωαδα αχρις ημερων πεντε ου διετριψαμεν ημερας επτα
transliteration: hmeiv de exepleusamen meta tav hmerav twn azumwn apo filippwn kai hlyomen prov autouv eiv thn trwada acriv hmerwn pente ou dietriqamen hmerav epta
draft_translation: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came to them at Troas in five days; where we remained seven days.
ukjv_translation: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.

greek_text: εν δε τη μια των σαββατων συνηγμενων των μαθητων του κλασαι αρτον ο παυλος διελεγετο αυτοις μελλων εξιεναι τη επαυριον παρετεινεν τε τον λογον μεχρι μεσονυκτιου
transliteration: en de th mia twn sabbatwn sunhgmenwn twn mayhtwn tou klasai arton o paulov dielegeto autoiv mellwn exienai th epaurion pareteinen te ton logon mecri mesonuktiou
draft_translation: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul reasoned with them, being ready to depart on the next day; and continued his speech until midnight.
ukjv_translation: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the next day; and continued his speech (o. logos) until midnight.

greek_text: ησαν δε λαμπαδες ικαναι εν τω υπερωω ου ησαν συνηγμενοι
transliteration: hsan de lampadev ikanai en tw uperww ou hsan sunhgmenoi
draft_translation: And there were many lamps in the upper room, where they were gathered together.
ukjv_translation: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.

greek_text: καθημενος δε τις νεανιας ονοματι ευτυχος επι της θυριδος καταφερομενος υπνω βαθει διαλεγομενου του παυλου επι πλειον κατενεχθεις απο του υπνου επεσεν απο του τριστεγου κατω και ηρθη νεκρος
transliteration: kayhmenov de tiv neaniav onomati eutucov epi thv yuridov kataferomenov upnw bayei dialegomenou tou paulou epi pleion katenecyeiv apo tou upnou epesen apo tou tristegou katw kai hryh nekrov
draft_translation: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being overcome with deep sleep: and as Paul was speaking long, he sank down with sleep, and fell down from the third story, and was taken up dead.
ukjv_translation: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third upper room, and was taken up dead.

greek_text: καταβας δε ο παυλος επεπεσεν αυτω και συμπεριλαβων ειπεν μη θορυβεισθε η γαρ ψυχη αυτου εν αυτω εστιν
transliteration: katabav de o paulov epepesen autw kai sumperilabwn eipen mh yorubeisye h gar quch autou en autw estin
draft_translation: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Do not be troubled; for his life is in him.
ukjv_translation: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

greek_text: αναβας δε και κλασας αρτον και γευσαμενος εφ ικανον τε ομιλησας αχρις αυγης ουτως εξηλθεν
transliteration: anabav de kai klasav arton kai geusamenov ef ikanon te omilhsav acriv aughv outwv exhlyen
draft_translation: When he therefore had come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till daybreak, so he departed.
ukjv_translation: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.

greek_text: ηγαγον δε τον παιδα ζωντα και παρεκληθησαν ου μετριως
transliteration: hgagon de ton paida zwnta kai pareklhyhsan ou metriwv
draft_translation: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
ukjv_translation: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.

greek_text: ημεις δε προελθοντες επι το πλοιον ανηχθημεν εις την ασσον εκειθεν μελλοντες αναλαμβανειν τον παυλον ουτως γαρ ην διατεταγμενος μελλων αυτος πεζευειν
transliteration: hmeiv de proelyontev epi to ploion anhcyhmen eiv thn asson ekeiyen mellontev analambanein ton paulon outwv gar hn diatetagmenov mellwn autov pezeuein
draft_translation: And we went on board the boat, and sailed to Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go on foot.
ukjv_translation: And we went on board ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go on foot.

greek_text: ως δε συνεβαλεν ημιν εις την ασσον αναλαβοντες αυτον ηλθομεν εις μιτυληνην
transliteration: wv de sunebalen hmin eiv thn asson analabontev auton hlyomen eiv mitulhnhn
draft_translation: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mytilene.
ukjv_translation: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.

greek_text: κακειθεν αποπλευσαντες τη επιουση κατηντησαμεν αντικρυ χιου τη δε ετερα παρεβαλομεν εις σαμον και μειναντες εν τρωγυλλιω τη εχομενη ηλθομεν εις μιλητον
transliteration: kakeiyen apopleusantev th epioush kathnthsamen antikru ciou th de etera parebalomen eiv samon kai meinantev en trwgulliw th ecomenh hlyomen eiv milhton
draft_translation: And we sailed from there, and came the next day opposite Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and remained at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
ukjv_translation: And we sailed thence, and came the next day opposite to Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.

greek_text: εκρινεν γαρ ο παυλος παραπλευσαι την εφεσον οπως μη γενηται αυτω χρονοτριβησαι εν τη ασια εσπευδεν γαρ ει δυνατον ην αυτω την ημεραν της πεντηκοστης γενεσθαι εις ιεροσολυμα
transliteration: ekrinen gar o paulov parapleusai thn efeson opwv mh genhtai autw cronotribhsai en th asia espeuden gar ei dunaton hn autw thn hmeran thv penthkosthv genesyai eiv ierosoluma
draft_translation: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, because he would not spend time in Asia: for he was hurrying, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
ukjv_translation: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.

greek_text: απο δε της μιλητου πεμψας εις εφεσον μετεκαλεσατο τους πρεσβυτερους της εκκλησιας
transliteration: apo de thv milhtou pemqav eiv efeson metekalesato touv presbuterouv thv ekklhsiav
draft_translation: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the assembly.
ukjv_translation: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.

greek_text: ως δε παρεγενοντο προς αυτον ειπεν αυτοις υμεις επιστασθε απο πρωτης ημερας αφ ης επεβην εις την ασιαν πως μεθ υμων τον παντα χρονον εγενομην
transliteration: wv de paregenonto prov auton eipen autoiv umeiv epistasye apo prwthv hmerav af hv epebhn eiv thn asian pwv mey umwn ton panta cronon egenomhn
draft_translation: And when they had come to him, he said to them, You know, from the first day that I came into Asia, how I have been with you at all times,
ukjv_translation: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, All of you know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,

greek_text: δουλευων τω κυριω μετα πασης ταπεινοφροσυνης και πολλων δακρυων και πειρασμων των συμβαντων μοι εν ταις επιβουλαις των ιουδαιων
transliteration: douleuwn tw kuriw meta pashv tapeinofrosunhv kai pollwn dakruwn kai peirasmwn twn sumbantwn moi en taiv epiboulaiv twn ioudaiwn
draft_translation: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and trials, which befell me by the plots of the Jews:
ukjv_translation: Serving the LORD with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:

greek_text: ως ουδεν υπεστειλαμην των συμφεροντων του μη αναγγειλαι υμιν και διδαξαι υμας δημοσια και κατ οικους
transliteration: wv ouden upesteilamhn twn sumferontwn tou mh anaggeilai umin kai didaxai umav dhmosia kai kat oikouv
draft_translation: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable to you, but have declared it to you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house,
ukjv_translation: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have showed you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house,

greek_text: διαμαρτυρομενος ιουδαιοις τε και ελλησιν την εις τον θεον μετανοιαν και πιστιν την εις τον κυριον ημων ιησουν χριστον
transliteration: diamarturomenov ioudaioiv te kai ellhsin thn eiv ton yeon metanoian kai pistin thn eiv ton kurion hmwn ihsoun criston
draft_translation: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
ukjv_translation: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.

greek_text: και νυν ιδου εγω δεδεμενος τω πνευματι πορευομαι εις ιερουσαλημ τα εν αυτη συναντησοντα μοι μη ειδως
transliteration: kai nun idou egw dedemenov tw pneumati poreuomai eiv ierousalhm ta en auth sunanthsonta moi mh eidwv
draft_translation: And now, look, I go bound in spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
ukjv_translation: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit (o. pneuma) unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:

greek_text: πλην οτι το πνευμα το αγιον κατα πολιν διαμαρτυρεται λεγον οτι δεσμα με και θλιψεις μενουσιν
transliteration: plhn oti to pneuma to agion kata polin diamarturetai legon oti desma me kai yliqeiv menousin
draft_translation: Except that the Holy Spirit witnesses in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.
ukjv_translation: Save that the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) witnesses in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

greek_text: αλλ ουδενος λογον ποιουμαι ουδε εχω την ψυχην μου τιμιαν εμαυτω ως τελειωσαι τον δρομον μου μετα χαρας και την διακονιαν ην ελαβον παρα του κυριου ιησου διαμαρτυρασθαι το ευαγγελιον της χαριτος του θεου
transliteration: all oudenov logon poioumai oude ecw thn quchn mou timian emautw wv teleiwsai ton dromon mou meta carav kai thn diakonian hn elabon para tou kuriou ihsou diamarturasyai to euaggelion thv caritov tou yeou
draft_translation: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear to myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the good news of the grace of God.
ukjv_translation: But none of these things (o. logos) move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; normalized NT kurios as Lord; removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker; rendered euangelion as good news

greek_text: και νυν ιδου εγω οιδα οτι ουκετι οψεσθε το προσωπον μου υμεις παντες εν οις διηλθον κηρυσσων την βασιλειαν του θεου
transliteration: kai nun idou egw oida oti ouketi oqesye to proswpon mou umeiv pantev en oiv dihlyon khrusswn thn basileian tou yeou
draft_translation: And now, look, I know that you all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
ukjv_translation: And now, behold, I know that all of you all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.

greek_text: διο μαρτυρομαι υμιν εν τη σημερον ημερα οτι καθαρος εγω απο του αιματος παντων
transliteration: dio marturomai umin en th shmeron hmera oti kayarov egw apo tou aimatov pantwn
draft_translation: Therefore I testify to you this day, that I am pure from the blood of all.
ukjv_translation: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.

greek_text: ου γαρ υπεστειλαμην του μη αναγγειλαι υμιν πασαν την βουλην του θεου
transliteration: ou gar upesteilamhn tou mh anaggeilai umin pasan thn boulhn tou yeou
draft_translation: For I did not shrink from declaring to you all the counsel of God.
ukjv_translation: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.

greek_text: προσεχετε ουν εαυτοις και παντι τω ποιμνιω εν ω υμας το πνευμα το αγιον εθετο επισκοπους ποιμαινειν την εκκλησιαν του θεου ην περιεποιησατο δια του ιδιου αιματος
transliteration: prosecete oun eautoiv kai panti tw poimniw en w umav to pneuma to agion eyeto episkopouv poimainein thn ekklhsian tou yeou hn periepoihsato dia tou idiou aimatov
draft_translation: Take heed therefore to yourselves, and to all the flock, over which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to feed the assembly of God, which he has purchased with his own blood.
ukjv_translation: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) has made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he has purchased with his own blood.
review_notes: fixed non-person relative after assembly; modernized archaic directional unto; modernized over-the-which wording; modernized personal which as who; removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker; rendered ekklesia as assembly

greek_text: εγω γαρ οιδα τουτο οτι εισελευσονται μετα την αφιξιν μου λυκοι βαρεις εις υμας μη φειδομενοι του ποιμνιου
transliteration: egw gar oida touto oti eiseleusontai meta thn afixin mou lukoi bareiv eiv umav mh feidomenoi tou poimniou
draft_translation: For I know this, that after my departure savage wolves shall enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
ukjv_translation: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

greek_text: και εξ υμων αυτων αναστησονται ανδρες λαλουντες διεστραμμενα του αποσπαν τους μαθητας οπισω αυτων
transliteration: kai ex umwn autwn anasthsontai andrev lalountev diestrammena tou apospan touv mayhtav opisw autwn
draft_translation: Also from among your own selves men shall arise, speaking distorted things, to draw away disciples after them.
ukjv_translation: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.

greek_text: διο γρηγορειτε μνημονευοντες οτι τριετιαν νυκτα και ημεραν ουκ επαυσαμην μετα δακρυων νουθετων ενα εκαστον
transliteration: dio grhgoreite mnhmoneuontev oti trietian nukta kai hmeran ouk epausamhn meta dakruwn nouyetwn ena ekaston
draft_translation: Therefore watch, and remember, that for three years, night and day, I did not cease to warn every one with tears.
ukjv_translation: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.

greek_text: και τα νυν παρατιθεμαι υμας αδελφοι τω θεω και τω λογω της χαριτος αυτου τω δυναμενω εποικοδομησαι και δουναι υμιν κληρονομιαν εν τοις ηγιασμενοις πασιν
transliteration: kai ta nun paratiyemai umav adelfoi tw yew kai tw logw thv caritov autou tw dunamenw epoikodomhsai kai dounai umin klhronomian en toiv hgiasmenoiv pasin
draft_translation: And now, brothers, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
ukjv_translation: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word (o. logos) of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.

greek_text: αργυριου η χρυσιου η ιματισμου ουδενος επεθυμησα
transliteration: arguriou h crusiou h imatismou oudenov epeyumhsa
draft_translation: I have desired no one's silver, or gold, or clothing.
ukjv_translation: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel.

greek_text: αυτοι δε γινωσκετε οτι ταις χρειαις μου και τοις ουσιν μετ εμου υπηρετησαν αι χειρες αυται
transliteration: autoi de ginwskete oti taiv creiaiv mou kai toiv ousin met emou uphrethsan ai ceirev autai
draft_translation: Yes, you yourselves know, that these hands have served my needs, and those who were with me.
ukjv_translation: Yea, all of you yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.

greek_text: παντα υπεδειξα υμιν οτι ουτως κοπιωντας δει αντιλαμβανεσθαι των ασθενουντων μνημονευειν τε των λογων του κυριου ιησου οτι αυτος ειπεν μακαριον εστιν διδοναι μαλλον η λαμβανειν
transliteration: panta upedeixa umin oti outwv kopiwntav dei antilambanesyai twn asyenountwn mnhmoneuein te twn logwn tou kuriou ihsou oti autov eipen makarion estin didonai mallon h lambanein
draft_translation: I have showed you all things, how that so laboring you ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
ukjv_translation: I have showed you all things, how that so labouring all of you ought to support the weak, and to remember the words (o. logos) of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
review_notes: modernized labour spelling; normalized NT kurios as Lord; removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker; removed UKJV plural-expansion artifact

greek_text: και ταυτα ειπων θεις τα γονατα αυτου συν πασιν αυτοις προσηυξατο
transliteration: kai tauta eipwn yeiv ta gonata autou sun pasin autoiv proshuxato
draft_translation: And when he had thus spoken, he knelt down, and prayed with them all.
ukjv_translation: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.

greek_text: ικανος δε εγενετο κλαυθμος παντων και επιπεσοντες επι τον τραχηλον του παυλου κατεφιλουν αυτον
transliteration: ikanov de egeneto klauymov pantwn kai epipesontev epi ton trachlon tou paulou katefiloun auton
draft_translation: And they all wept greatly, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him,
ukjv_translation: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him,

greek_text: οδυνωμενοι μαλιστα επι τω λογω ω ειρηκει οτι ουκετι μελλουσιν το προσωπον αυτου θεωρειν προεπεμπον δε αυτον εις το πλοιον
transliteration: odunwmenoi malista epi tw logw w eirhkei oti ouketi mellousin to proswpon autou yewrein proepempon de auton eiv to ploion
draft_translation: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spoke, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the boat.
ukjv_translation: Sorrowing most of all for the words (o. logos) which he spoke, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: ως δε εγενετο αναχθηναι ημας αποσπασθεντας απ αυτων ευθυδρομησαντες ηλθομεν εις την κων τη δε εξης εις την ροδον κακειθεν εις παταρα
transliteration: wv de egeneto anacyhnai hmav apospasyentav ap autwn euyudromhsantev hlyomen eiv thn kwn th de exhv eiv thn rodon kakeiyen eiv patara
draft_translation: And it happened, that after we were torn away from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara:
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass, that after we were got from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:

greek_text: και ευροντες πλοιον διαπερων εις φοινικην επιβαντες ανηχθημεν
transliteration: kai eurontev ploion diaperwn eiv foinikhn epibantev anhcyhmen
draft_translation: And finding a boat sailing over to Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
ukjv_translation: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: αναφαναντες δε την κυπρον και καταλιποντες αυτην ευωνυμον επλεομεν εις συριαν και κατηχθημεν εις τυρον εκεισε γαρ ην το πλοιον αποφορτιζομενον τον γομον
transliteration: anafanantev de thn kupron kai katalipontev authn euwnumon epleomen eiv surian kai kathcyhmen eiv turon ekeise gar hn to ploion apofortizomenon ton gomon
draft_translation: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the boat was to unload her burden.
ukjv_translation: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unload her burden.

greek_text: και ανευροντες μαθητας επεμειναμεν αυτου ημερας επτα οιτινες τω παυλω ελεγον δια του πνευματος μη αναβαινειν εις ιερουσαλημ
transliteration: kai aneurontev mayhtav epemeinamen autou hmerav epta oitinev tw paulw elegon dia tou pneumatov mh anabainein eiv ierousalhm
draft_translation: And finding disciples, we stayed there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
ukjv_translation: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, (o. pneuma) that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

greek_text: οτε δε εγενετο ημας εξαρτισαι τας ημερας εξελθοντες επορευομεθα προπεμποντων ημας παντων συν γυναιξιν και τεκνοις εως εξω της πολεως και θεντες τα γονατα επι τον αιγιαλον προσηυξαμεθα
transliteration: ote de egeneto hmav exartisai tav hmerav exelyontev eporeuomeya propempontwn hmav pantwn sun gunaixin kai teknoiv ewv exw thv polewv kai yentev ta gonata epi ton aigialon proshuxameya
draft_translation: And when we had completed those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we knelt down on the shore, and prayed.
ukjv_translation: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

greek_text: και ασπασαμενοι αλληλους επεβημεν εις το πλοιον εκεινοι δε υπεστρεψαν εις τα ιδια
transliteration: kai aspasamenoi allhlouv epebhmen eiv to ploion ekeinoi de upestreqan eiv ta idia
draft_translation: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we boarded the boat; and they returned home again.
ukjv_translation: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.

greek_text: ημεις δε τον πλουν διανυσαντες απο τυρου κατηντησαμεν εις πτολεμαιδα και ασπασαμενοι τους αδελφους εμειναμεν ημεραν μιαν παρ αυτοις
transliteration: hmeiv de ton ploun dianusantev apo turou kathnthsamen eiv ptolemaida kai aspasamenoi touv adelfouv emeinamen hmeran mian par autoiv
draft_translation: And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and greeted the brothers, and remained with them one day.
ukjv_translation: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

greek_text: τη δε επαυριον εξελθοντες οι περι τον παυλον ηλθομεν εις καισαρειαν και εισελθοντες εις τον οικον φιλιππου του ευαγγελιστου του οντος εκ των επτα εμειναμεν παρ αυτω
transliteration: th de epaurion exelyontev oi peri ton paulon hlyomen eiv kaisareian kai eiselyontev eiv ton oikon filippou tou euaggelistou tou ontov ek twn epta emeinamen par autw
draft_translation: And the next day we who were of Paul's company departed, and came to Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven; and remained with him.
ukjv_translation: And the next day we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.

greek_text: τουτω δε ησαν θυγατερες παρθενοι τεσσαρες προφητευουσαι
transliteration: toutw de hsan yugaterev paryenoi tessarev profhteuousai
draft_translation: And the same man had four virgin daughters, who prophesied.
ukjv_translation: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.

greek_text: επιμενοντων δε ημων ημερας πλειους κατηλθεν τις απο της ιουδαιας προφητης ονοματι αγαβος
transliteration: epimenontwn de hmwn hmerav pleiouv kathlyen tiv apo thv ioudaiav profhthv onomati agabov
draft_translation: And as we stayed there many days, there came down from Judea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
ukjv_translation: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.

greek_text: και ελθων προς ημας και αρας την ζωνην του παυλου δησας τε αυτου τας χειρας και τους ποδας ειπεν ταδε λεγει το πνευμα το αγιον τον ανδρα ου εστιν η ζωνη αυτη ουτως δησουσιν εν ιερουσαλημ οι ιουδαιοι και παραδωσουσιν εις χειρας εθνων
transliteration: kai elywn prov hmav kai arav thn zwnhn tou paulou dhsav te autou tav ceirav kai touv podav eipen tade legei to pneuma to agion ton andra ou estin h zwnh auth outwv dhsousin en ierousalhm oi ioudaioi kai paradwsousin eiv ceirav eynwn
draft_translation: And when he had come to us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus says the Holy Spirit, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owns this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the nations.
ukjv_translation: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus says the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owns this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized was-come perfect; removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker; rendered ethne as nations

greek_text: ως δε ηκουσαμεν ταυτα παρεκαλουμεν ημεις τε και οι εντοπιοι του μη αναβαινειν αυτον εις ιερουσαλημ
transliteration: wv de hkousamen tauta parekaloumen hmeiv te kai oi entopioi tou mh anabainein auton eiv ierousalhm
draft_translation: And when we heard these things, both we, and those of that place, begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.
ukjv_translation: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.

greek_text: απεκριθη δε ο παυλος τι ποιειτε κλαιοντες και συνθρυπτοντες μου την καρδιαν εγω γαρ ου μονον δεθηναι αλλα και αποθανειν εις ιερουσαλημ ετοιμως εχω υπερ του ονοματος του κυριου ιησου
transliteration: apekriyh de o paulov ti poieite klaiontev kai sunyruptontev mou thn kardian egw gar ou monon deyhnai alla kai apoyanein eiv ierousalhm etoimwv ecw uper tou onomatov tou kuriou ihsou
draft_translation: Then Paul answered, What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? for I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
ukjv_translation: Then Paul answered, What mean all of you to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

greek_text: μη πειθομενου δε αυτου ησυχασαμεν ειποντες το θελημα του κυριου γενεσθω
transliteration: mh peiyomenou de autou hsucasamen eipontev to yelhma tou kuriou genesyw
draft_translation: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
ukjv_translation: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.

greek_text: μετα δε τας ημερας ταυτας αποσκευασαμενοι ανεβαινομεν εις ιερουσαλημ
transliteration: meta de tav hmerav tautav aposkeuasamenoi anebainomen eiv ierousalhm
draft_translation: And after those days we packed our baggage, and went up to Jerusalem.
ukjv_translation: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.

greek_text: συνηλθον δε και των μαθητων απο καισαρειας συν ημιν αγοντες παρ ω ξενισθωμεν μνασωνι τινι κυπριω αρχαιω μαθητη
transliteration: sunhlyon de kai twn mayhtwn apo kaisareiav sun hmin agontev par w xenisywmen mnaswni tini kupriw arcaiw mayhth
draft_translation: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, bringing us to Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we should lodge.
ukjv_translation: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.

greek_text: γενομενων δε ημων εις ιεροσολυμα ασμενως εδεξαντο ημας οι αδελφοι
transliteration: genomenwn de hmwn eiv ierosoluma asmenwv edexanto hmav oi adelfoi
draft_translation: And when we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
ukjv_translation: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.

greek_text: τη δε επιουση εισηει ο παυλος συν ημιν προς ιακωβον παντες τε παρεγενοντο οι πρεσβυτεροι
transliteration: th de epioush eishei o paulov sun hmin prov iakwbon pantev te paregenonto oi presbuteroi
draft_translation: And the day following Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.
ukjv_translation: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.

greek_text: και ασπασαμενος αυτους εξηγειτο καθ εν εκαστον ων εποιησεν ο θεος εν τοις εθνεσιν δια της διακονιας αυτου
transliteration: kai aspasamenov autouv exhgeito kay en ekaston wn epoihsen o yeov en toiv eynesin dia thv diakoniav autou
draft_translation: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had worked among the nations by his ministry.
ukjv_translation: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
review_notes: modernized wrought; rendered ethne as nations

greek_text: οι δε ακουσαντες εδοξαζον τον κυριον ειπον τε αυτω θεωρεις αδελφε ποσαι μυριαδες εισιν ιουδαιων των πεπιστευκοτων και παντες ζηλωται του νομου υπαρχουσιν
transliteration: oi de akousantev edoxazon ton kurion eipon te autw yewreiv adelfe posai muriadev eisin ioudaiwn twn pepisteukotwn kai pantev zhlwtai tou nomou uparcousin
draft_translation: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said to him, You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are who believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
ukjv_translation: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized personal which as who; normalized NT kurios as Lord

greek_text: κατηχηθησαν δε περι σου οτι αποστασιαν διδασκεις απο μωσεως τους κατα τα εθνη παντας ιουδαιους λεγων μη περιτεμνειν αυτους τα τεκνα μηδε τοις εθεσιν περιπατειν
transliteration: kathchyhsan de peri sou oti apostasian didaskeiv apo mwsewv touv kata ta eynh pantav ioudaiouv legwn mh peritemnein autouv ta tekna mhde toiv eyesin peripatein
draft_translation: And they are informed of you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the nations to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
ukjv_translation: And they are informed of you, that you teach all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
review_notes: modernized personal which as who; rendered ethne as nations

greek_text: τι ουν εστιν παντως δει πληθος συνελθειν ακουσονται γαρ οτι εληλυθας
transliteration: ti oun estin pantwv dei plhyov sunelyein akousontai gar oti elhluyav
draft_translation: What is it therefore? the multitude must come together: for they will hear that you have come.
ukjv_translation: What is it therefore? the multitude must essentially come together: for they will hear that you are come.
review_notes: cleaned must-essentially source artifact; modernized are-come perfect

greek_text: τουτο ουν ποιησον ο σοι λεγομεν εισιν ημιν ανδρες τεσσαρες ευχην εχοντες εφ εαυτων
transliteration: touto oun poihson o soi legomen eisin hmin andrev tessarev euchn econtev ef eautwn
draft_translation: Do therefore this that we say to you: We have four men who have a vow on themselves;
ukjv_translation: Do therefore this that we say to you: We have four men which have a vow on them;

greek_text: τουτους παραλαβων αγνισθητι συν αυτοις και δαπανησον επ αυτοις ινα ξυρησωνται την κεφαλην και γνωσιν παντες οτι ων κατηχηνται περι σου ουδεν εστιν αλλα στοιχεις και αυτος τον νομον φυλασσων
transliteration: toutouv paralabwn agnisyhti sun autoiv kai dapanhson ep autoiv ina xurhswntai thn kefalhn kai gnwsin pantev oti wn kathchntai peri sou ouden estin alla stoiceiv kai autov ton nomon fulasswn
draft_translation: Take them, and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, of which they were informed concerning you, are nothing; but that you yourself also walk orderly, keeping the law.
ukjv_translation: Them take, and purify yourself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning you, are nothing; but that you yourself also walk orderly, and keep the law.

greek_text: περι δε των πεπιστευκοτων εθνων ημεις επεστειλαμεν κριναντες μηδεν τοιουτον τηρειν αυτους ει μη φυλασσεσθαι αυτους το τε ειδωλοθυτον και το αιμα και πνικτον και πορνειαν
transliteration: peri de twn pepisteukotwn eynwn hmeiv epesteilamen krinantev mhden toiouton threin autouv ei mh fulassesyai autouv to te eidwloyuton kai to aima kai pnikton kai porneian
draft_translation: As concerning the nations that believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from sexual immorality.
ukjv_translation: As concerning the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
review_notes: modernized nations relative as that; modernized porneia wording; rendered ethne as nations

greek_text: τοτε ο παυλος παραλαβων τους ανδρας τη εχομενη ημερα συν αυτοις αγνισθεις εισηει εις το ιερον διαγγελλων την εκπληρωσιν των ημερων του αγνισμου εως ου προσηνεχθη υπερ ενος εκαστου αυτων η προσφορα
transliteration: tote o paulov paralabwn touv andrav th ecomenh hmera sun autoiv agnisyeiv eishei eiv to ieron diaggellwn thn ekplhrwsin twn hmerwn tou agnismou ewv ou proshnecyh uper enov ekastou autwn h prosfora
draft_translation: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, declaring the completion of the days of purification, until the offering should be offered for every one of them.
ukjv_translation: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.

greek_text: ως δε εμελλον αι επτα ημεραι συντελεισθαι οι απο της ασιας ιουδαιοι θεασαμενοι αυτον εν τω ιερω συνεχεον παντα τον οχλον και επεβαλον τας χειρας επ αυτον
transliteration: wv de emellon ai epta hmerai sunteleisyai oi apo thv asiav ioudaioi yeasamenoi auton en tw ierw suneceon panta ton oclon kai epebalon tav ceirav ep auton
draft_translation: And when the seven days were almost completed, the Jews who were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
ukjv_translation: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

greek_text: κραζοντες ανδρες ισραηλιται βοηθειτε ουτος εστιν ο ανθρωπος ο κατα του λαου και του νομου και του τοπου τουτου παντας πανταχου διδασκων ετι τε και ελληνας εισηγαγεν εις το ιερον και κεκοινωκεν τον αγιον τοπον τουτον
transliteration: krazontev andrev israhlitai bohyeite outov estin o anyrwpov o kata tou laou kai tou nomou kai tou topou toutou pantav pantacou didaskwn eti te kai ellhnav eishgagen eiv to ieron kai kekoinwken ton agion topon touton
draft_translation: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man that teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and has defiled this holy place.
ukjv_translation: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teaches all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and has polluted this holy place.

greek_text: ησαν γαρ προεωρακοτες τροφιμον τον εφεσιον εν τη πολει συν αυτω ον ενομιζον οτι εις το ιερον εισηγαγεν ο παυλος
transliteration: hsan gar proewrakotev trofimon ton efesion en th polei sun autw on enomizon oti eiv to ieron eishgagen o paulov
draft_translation: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
ukjv_translation: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

greek_text: εκινηθη τε η πολις ολη και εγενετο συνδρομη του λαου και επιλαβομενοι του παυλου ειλκον αυτον εξω του ιερου και ευθεως εκλεισθησαν αι θυραι
transliteration: ekinhyh te h poliv olh kai egeneto sundromh tou laou kai epilabomenoi tou paulou eilkon auton exw tou ierou kai euyewv ekleisyhsan ai yurai
draft_translation: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and immediately the doors were shut.
ukjv_translation: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.

greek_text: ζητουντων δε αυτον αποκτειναι ανεβη φασις τω χιλιαρχω της σπειρης οτι ολη συγκεχυται ιερουσαλημ
transliteration: zhtountwn de auton apokteinai anebh fasiv tw ciliarcw thv speirhv oti olh sugkecutai ierousalhm
draft_translation: And as they sought to kill him, a report came to the commander of the cohort, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
ukjv_translation: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

greek_text: ος εξαυτης παραλαβων στρατιωτας και εκατονταρχους κατεδραμεν επ αυτους οι δε ιδοντες τον χιλιαρχον και τους στρατιωτας επαυσαντο τυπτοντες τον παυλον
transliteration: ov exauthv paralabwn stratiwtav kai ekatontarcouv katedramen ep autouv oi de idontev ton ciliarcon kai touv stratiwtav epausanto tuptontev ton paulon
draft_translation: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them: and when they saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
ukjv_translation: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.

greek_text: τοτε εγγισας ο χιλιαρχος επελαβετο αυτου και εκελευσεν δεθηναι αλυσεσιν δυσιν και επυνθανετο τις αν ειη και τι εστιν πεποιηκως
transliteration: tote eggisav o ciliarcov epelabeto autou kai ekeleusen deyhnai alusesin dusin kai epunyaneto tiv an eih kai ti estin pepoihkwv
draft_translation: Then the commander came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and inquired who he was, and what he had done.
ukjv_translation: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

greek_text: αλλοι δε αλλο τι εβοων εν τω οχλω μη δυναμενος δε γνωναι το ασφαλες δια τον θορυβον εκελευσεν αγεσθαι αυτον εις την παρεμβολην
transliteration: alloi de allo ti ebown en tw oclw mh dunamenov de gnwnai to asfalev dia ton yorubon ekeleusen agesyai auton eiv thn parembolhn
draft_translation: And some cried one thing, some another, among the crowd: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the barracks.
ukjv_translation: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.

greek_text: οτε δε εγενετο επι τους αναβαθμους συνεβη βασταζεσθαι αυτον υπο των στρατιωτων δια την βιαν του οχλου
transliteration: ote de egeneto epi touv anabaymouv sunebh bastazesyai auton upo twn stratiwtwn dia thn bian tou oclou
draft_translation: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the people.
ukjv_translation: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.

greek_text: ηκολουθει γαρ το πληθος του λαου κραζον αιρε αυτον
transliteration: hkolouyei gar to plhyov tou laou krazon aire auton
draft_translation: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
ukjv_translation: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.

greek_text: μελλων τε εισαγεσθαι εις την παρεμβολην ο παυλος λεγει τω χιλιαρχω ει εξεστιν μοι ειπειν τι προς σε ο δε εφη ελληνιστι γινωσκεις
transliteration: mellwn te eisagesyai eiv thn parembolhn o paulov legei tw ciliarcw ei exestin moi eipein ti prov se o de efh ellhnisti ginwskeiv
draft_translation: And as Paul was to be led into the barracks, he said to the commander, May I speak to you? Who said, Can you speak Greek?
ukjv_translation: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto you? Who said, Can you speak Greek?

greek_text: ουκ αρα συ ει ο αιγυπτιος ο προ τουτων των ημερων αναστατωσας και εξαγαγων εις την ερημον τους τετρακισχιλιους ανδρας των σικαριων
transliteration: ouk ara su ei o aiguptiov o pro toutwn twn hmerwn anastatwsav kai exagagwn eiv thn erhmon touv tetrakisciliouv andrav twn sikariwn
draft_translation: Are you not that Egyptian, who before these days made an uproar, and led out into the wilderness four thousand men of the assassins?
ukjv_translation: Are not you that Egyptian, which before these days made an uproar, and led out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?

greek_text: ειπεν δε ο παυλος εγω ανθρωπος μεν ειμι ιουδαιος ταρσευς της κιλικιας ουκ ασημου πολεως πολιτης δεομαι δε σου επιτρεψον μοι λαλησαι προς τον λαον
transliteration: eipen de o paulov egw anyrwpov men eimi ioudaiov tarseuv thv kilikiav ouk ashmou polewv polithv deomai de sou epitreqon moi lalhsai prov ton laon
draft_translation: But Paul said, I am a Jewish man of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city: and, I ask you, permit me to speak to the people.
ukjv_translation: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I plead to you, suffer me to speak unto the people.

greek_text: επιτρεψαντος δε αυτου ο παυλος εστως επι των αναβαθμων κατεσεισεν τη χειρι τω λαω πολλης δε σιγης γενομενης προσεφωνησεν τη εβραιδι διαλεκτω λεγων
transliteration: epitreqantov de autou o paulov estwv epi twn anabaymwn kateseisen th ceiri tw law pollhv de sighv genomenhv prosefwnhsen th ebraidi dialektw legwn
draft_translation: And when he had given him permission, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand to the people. And when there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew dialect, saying,
ukjv_translation: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spoke unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,

greek_text: ανδρες αδελφοι και πατερες ακουσατε μου της προς υμας νυν απολογιας
transliteration: andrev adelfoi kai paterev akousate mou thv prov umav nun apologiav
draft_translation: Men, brothers, and fathers, hear my defense which I now make to you.
ukjv_translation: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear all of you my defence which I make now unto you.

greek_text: ακουσαντες δε οτι τη εβραιδι διαλεκτω προσεφωνει αυτοις μαλλον παρεσχον ησυχιαν και φησιν
transliteration: akousantev de oti th ebraidi dialektw prosefwnei autoiv mallon parescon hsucian kai fhsin
draft_translation: (And when they heard that he spoke in the Hebrew dialect to them, they kept more silence: and he says,)
ukjv_translation: (And when they heard that he spoke in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he says,)

greek_text: εγω μεν ειμι ανηρ ιουδαιος γεγεννημενος εν ταρσω της κιλικιας ανατεθραμμενος δε εν τη πολει ταυτη παρα τους ποδας γαμαλιηλ πεπαιδευμενος κατα ακριβειαν του πατρωου νομου ζηλωτης υπαρχων του θεου καθως παντες υμεις εστε σημερον
transliteration: egw men eimi anhr ioudaiov gegennhmenov en tarsw thv kilikiav anateyrammenov de en th polei tauth para touv podav gamalihl pepaideumenov kata akribeian tou patrwou nomou zhlwthv uparcwn tou yeou kaywv pantev umeiv este shmeron
draft_translation: I am indeed a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, taught according to the strictness of the ancestral law, being zealous for God, as you all are this day.
ukjv_translation: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as all of you all are this day.

greek_text: ος ταυτην την οδον εδιωξα αχρι θανατου δεσμευων και παραδιδους εις φυλακας ανδρας τε και γυναικας
transliteration: ov tauthn thn odon ediwxa acri yanatou desmeuwn kai paradidouv eiv fulakav andrav te kai gunaikav
draft_translation: And I persecuted this Way to death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
ukjv_translation: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

greek_text: ως και ο αρχιερευς μαρτυρει μοι και παν το πρεσβυτεριον παρ ων και επιστολας δεξαμενος προς τους αδελφους εις δαμασκον επορευομην αξων και τους εκεισε οντας δεδεμενους εις ιερουσαλημ ινα τιμωρηθωσιν
transliteration: wv kai o arciereuv marturei moi kai pan to presbuterion par wn kai epistolav dexamenov prov touv adelfouv eiv damaskon eporeuomhn axwn kai touv ekeise ontav dedemenouv eiv ierousalhm ina timwrhywsin
draft_translation: As also the high priest bears me witness, and all the council of elders: from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and went to Damascus, to bring those who were there bound to Jerusalem, that they might be punished.
ukjv_translation: As also the high priest does bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, in order to be punished.

greek_text: εγενετο δε μοι πορευομενω και εγγιζοντι τη δαμασκω περι μεσημβριαν εξαιφνης εκ του ουρανου περιαστραψαι φως ικανον περι εμε
transliteration: egeneto de moi poreuomenw kai eggizonti th damaskw peri meshmbrian exaifnhv ek tou ouranou periastraqai fwv ikanon peri eme
draft_translation: And it happened, that, as I journeyed and drew near to Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light around me.
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

greek_text: επεσον τε εις το εδαφος και ηκουσα φωνης λεγουσης μοι σαουλ σαουλ τι με διωκεις
transliteration: epeson te eiv to edafov kai hkousa fwnhv legoushv moi saoul saoul ti me diwkeiv
draft_translation: And I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
ukjv_translation: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me?

greek_text: εγω δε απεκριθην τις ει κυριε ειπεν τε προς με εγω ειμι ιησους ο ναζωραιος ον συ διωκεις
transliteration: egw de apekriyhn tiv ei kurie eipen te prov me egw eimi ihsouv o nazwraiov on su diwkeiv
draft_translation: And I answered, Who are you, Lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.
ukjv_translation: And I answered, Who are you, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; normalized NT kurios as Lord

greek_text: οι δε συν εμοι οντες το μεν φως εθεασαντο και εμφοβοι εγενοντο την δε φωνην ουκ ηκουσαν του λαλουντος μοι
transliteration: oi de sun emoi ontev to men fwv eyeasanto kai emfoboi egenonto thn de fwnhn ouk hkousan tou lalountov moi
draft_translation: And those who were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they did not hear the voice of the one who spoke to me.
ukjv_translation: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spoke to me.

greek_text: ειπον δε τι ποιησω κυριε ο δε κυριος ειπεν προς με αναστας πορευου εις δαμασκον κακει σοι λαληθησεται περι παντων ων τετακται σοι ποιησαι
transliteration: eipon de ti poihsw kurie o de kuriov eipen prov me anastav poreuou eiv damaskon kakei soi lalhyhsetai peri pantwn wn tetaktai soi poihsai
draft_translation: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told you of all things which are appointed for you to do.
ukjv_translation: And I said, What shall I do, LORD? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told you of all things which are appointed for you to do.

greek_text: ως δε ουκ ενεβλεπον απο της δοξης του φωτος εκεινου χειραγωγουμενος υπο των συνοντων μοι ηλθον εις δαμασκον
transliteration: wv de ouk eneblepon apo thv doxhv tou fwtov ekeinou ceiragwgoumenov upo twn sunontwn moi hlyon eiv damaskon
draft_translation: And when I could not see because of the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.
ukjv_translation: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.

greek_text: ανανιας δε τις ανηρ ευσεβης κατα τον νομον μαρτυρουμενος υπο παντων των κατοικουντων ιουδαιων
transliteration: ananiav de tiv anhr eusebhv kata ton nomon marturoumenov upo pantwn twn katoikountwn ioudaiwn
draft_translation: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who dwelt there,
ukjv_translation: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,

greek_text: ελθων προς με και επιστας ειπεν μοι σαουλ αδελφε αναβλεψον καγω αυτη τη ωρα ανεβλεψα εις αυτον
transliteration: elywn prov me kai epistav eipen moi saoul adelfe anableqon kagw auth th wra anebleqa eiv auton
draft_translation: Came to me, and stood, and said to me, Brother Saul, receive your sight. And the same hour I looked up at him.
ukjv_translation: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive your sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.

greek_text: ο δε ειπεν ο θεος των πατερων ημων προεχειρισατο σε γνωναι το θελημα αυτου και ιδειν τον δικαιον και ακουσαι φωνην εκ του στοματος αυτου
transliteration: o de eipen o yeov twn paterwn hmwn proeceirisato se gnwnai to yelhma autou kai idein ton dikaion kai akousai fwnhn ek tou stomatov autou
draft_translation: And he said, The God of our fathers has chosen you, that you should know his will, and see the Righteous One, and should hear the voice from his mouth.
ukjv_translation: And he said, The God of our fathers has chosen you, that you should know his will, and see that Just One, and should hear the voice of his mouth.

greek_text: οτι εση μαρτυς αυτω προς παντας ανθρωπους ων εωρακας και ηκουσας
transliteration: oti esh martuv autw prov pantav anyrwpouv wn ewrakav kai hkousav
draft_translation: For you shall be his witness to all people of what you have seen and heard.
ukjv_translation: For you shall be his witness unto all men of what you have seen and heard.

greek_text: και νυν τι μελλεις αναστας βαπτισαι και απολουσαι τας αμαρτιας σου επικαλεσαμενος το ονομα του κυριου
transliteration: kai nun ti melleiv anastav baptisai kai apolousai tav amartiav sou epikalesamenov to onoma tou kuriou
draft_translation: And now why do you delay? arise, and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
ukjv_translation: And now why tarry you? arise, and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

greek_text: εγενετο δε μοι υποστρεψαντι εις ιερουσαλημ και προσευχομενου μου εν τω ιερω γενεσθαι με εν εκστασει
transliteration: egeneto de moi upostreqanti eiv ierousalhm kai proseucomenou mou en tw ierw genesyai me en ekstasei
draft_translation: And it happened, that, when I had returned to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
ukjv_translation: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;

greek_text: και ιδειν αυτον λεγοντα μοι σπευσον και εξελθε εν ταχει εξ ιερουσαλημ διοτι ου παραδεξονται σου την μαρτυριαν περι εμου
transliteration: kai idein auton legonta moi speuson kai exelye en tacei ex ierousalhm dioti ou paradexontai sou thn marturian peri emou
draft_translation: And saw him saying to me, Hurry, and get quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive your testimony concerning me.
ukjv_translation: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get you quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive your testimony concerning me.

greek_text: καγω ειπον κυριε αυτοι επιστανται οτι εγω ημην φυλακιζων και δερων κατα τας συναγωγας τους πιστευοντας επι σε
transliteration: kagw eipon kurie autoi epistantai oti egw hmhn fulakizwn kai derwn kata tav sunagwgav touv pisteuontav epi se
draft_translation: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed on you:
ukjv_translation: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on you:
review_notes: modernized them-that relative; normalized NT kurios as Lord

greek_text: και οτε εξεχειτο το αιμα στεφανου του μαρτυρος σου και αυτος ημην εφεστως και συνευδοκων τη αναιρεσει αυτου και φυλασσων τα ιματια των αναιρουντων αυτον
transliteration: kai ote execeito to aima stefanou tou marturov sou kai autov hmhn efestwv kai suneudokwn th anairesei autou kai fulasswn ta imatia twn anairountwn auton
draft_translation: And when the blood of your witness Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting to his death, and kept the clothing of those who killed him.
ukjv_translation: And when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.

greek_text: και ειπεν προς με πορευου οτι εγω εις εθνη μακραν εξαποστελω σε
transliteration: kai eipen prov me poreuou oti egw eiv eynh makran exapostelw se
draft_translation: And he said to me, Depart: for I will send you far away to the nations.
ukjv_translation: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send you far behind unto the Gentiles.

greek_text: ηκουον δε αυτου αχρι τουτου του λογου και επηραν την φωνην αυτων λεγοντες αιρε απο της γης τον τοιουτον ου γαρ καθηκον αυτον ζην
transliteration: hkouon de autou acri toutou tou logou kai ephran thn fwnhn autwn legontev aire apo thv ghv ton toiouton ou gar kayhkon auton zhn
draft_translation: And they listened to him until this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a man from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
ukjv_translation: And they gave him audience unto this word, (o. logos) and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

greek_text: κραυγαζοντων δε αυτων και ριπτουντων τα ιματια και κονιορτον βαλλοντων εις τον αερα
transliteration: kraugazontwn de autwn kai riptountwn ta imatia kai koniorton ballontwn eiv ton aera
draft_translation: And as they cried out, and threw off their clothes, and cast dust into the air,
ukjv_translation: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,

greek_text: εκελευσεν αυτον ο χιλιαρχος αγεσθαι εις την παρεμβολην ειπων μαστιξιν ανεταζεσθαι αυτον ινα επιγνω δι ην αιτιαν ουτως επεφωνουν αυτω
transliteration: ekeleusen auton o ciliarcov agesyai eiv thn parembolhn eipwn mastixin anetazesyai auton ina epignw di hn aitian outwv epefwnoun autw
draft_translation: The commander commanded him to be brought into the barracks, and ordered that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know why they cried so against him.
ukjv_translation: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

greek_text: ως δε προετειναν αυτον τοις ιμασιν ειπεν προς τον εστωτα εκατονταρχον ο παυλος ει ανθρωπον ρωμαιον και ακατακριτον εξεστιν υμιν μαστιζειν
transliteration: wv de proeteinan auton toiv imasin eipen prov ton estwta ekatontarcon o paulov ei anyrwpon rwmaion kai akatakriton exestin umin mastizein
draft_translation: And as they stretched him out with straps, Paul said to the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
ukjv_translation: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

greek_text: ακουσας δε ο εκατονταρχος προσελθων απηγγειλεν τω χιλιαρχω λεγων ορα τι μελλεις ποιειν ο γαρ ανθρωπος ουτος ρωμαιος εστιν
transliteration: akousav de o ekatontarcov proselywn aphggeilen tw ciliarcw legwn ora ti melleiv poiein o gar anyrwpov outov rwmaiov estin
draft_translation: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the commander, saying, Take care what you are about to do: for this man is a Roman.
ukjv_translation: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what you do: for this man is a Roman.

greek_text: προσελθων δε ο χιλιαρχος ειπεν αυτω λεγε μοι ει συ ρωμαιος ει ο δε εφη ναι
transliteration: proselywn de o ciliarcov eipen autw lege moi ei su rwmaiov ei o de efh nai
draft_translation: Then the commander came, and said to him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yes.
ukjv_translation: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, are you a Roman? He said, Yea.

greek_text: απεκριθη τε ο χιλιαρχος εγω πολλου κεφαλαιου την πολιτειαν ταυτην εκτησαμην ο δε παυλος εφη εγω δε και γεγεννημαι
transliteration: apekriyh te o ciliarcov egw pollou kefalaiou thn politeian tauthn ekthsamhn o de paulov efh egw de kai gegennhmai
draft_translation: And the commander answered, With a great sum I obtained this citizenship. And Paul said, But I was born a citizen.
ukjv_translation: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.

greek_text: ευθεως ουν απεστησαν απ αυτου οι μελλοντες αυτον ανεταζειν και ο χιλιαρχος δε εφοβηθη επιγνους οτι ρωμαιος εστιν και οτι ην αυτον δεδεκως
transliteration: euyewv oun apesthsan ap autou oi mellontev auton anetazein kai o ciliarcov de efobhyh epignouv oti rwmaiov estin kai oti hn auton dedekwv
draft_translation: Then immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
ukjv_translation: Then immediately they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
review_notes: fixed Acts 22:29 relative artifact; modernized him-which relative

greek_text: τη δε επαυριον βουλομενος γνωναι το ασφαλες το τι κατηγορειται παρα των ιουδαιων ελυσεν αυτον απο των δεσμων και εκελευσεν ελθειν τους αρχιερεις και ολον το συνεδριον αυτων και καταγαγων τον παυλον εστησεν εις αυτους
transliteration: th de epaurion boulomenov gnwnai to asfalev to ti kathgoreitai para twn ioudaiwn elusen auton apo twn desmwn kai ekeleusen elyein touv arciereiv kai olon to sunedrion autwn kai katagagwn ton paulon esthsen eiv autouv
draft_translation: On the next day, because he wanted to know with certainty why he was accused by the Jews, he loosed him from his bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to come, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
ukjv_translation: On the next day, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.

greek_text: ατενισας δε ο παυλος τω συνεδριω ειπεν ανδρες αδελφοι εγω παση συνειδησει αγαθη πεπολιτευμαι τω θεω αχρι ταυτης της ημερας
transliteration: atenisav de o paulov tw sunedriw eipen andrev adelfoi egw pash suneidhsei agayh pepoliteumai tw yew acri tauthv thv hmerav
draft_translation: And Paul, looking intently at the council, said, Men, brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until this day.
ukjv_translation: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

greek_text: ο δε αρχιερευς ανανιας επεταξεν τοις παρεστωσιν αυτω τυπτειν αυτου το στομα
transliteration: o de arciereuv ananiav epetaxen toiv parestwsin autw tuptein autou to stoma
draft_translation: And the high priest Ananias commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
ukjv_translation: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

greek_text: τοτε ο παυλος προς αυτον ειπεν τυπτειν σε μελλει ο θεος τοιχε κεκονιαμενε και συ καθη κρινων με κατα τον νομον και παρανομων κελευεις με τυπτεσθαι
transliteration: tote o paulov prov auton eipen tuptein se mellei o yeov toice kekoniamene kai su kayh krinwn me kata ton nomon kai paranomwn keleueiv me tuptesyai
draft_translation: Then Paul said to him, God shall strike you, you whitewashed wall: for are you sitting to judge me according to the law, and commanding me to be struck contrary to the law?
ukjv_translation: Then said Paul unto him, God shall strike you, you whitewashed wall: for sit you to judge me after the law, and command me to be smitten contrary to the law?

greek_text: οι δε παρεστωτες ειπον τον αρχιερεα του θεου λοιδορεις
transliteration: oi de parestwtev eipon ton arcierea tou yeou loidoreiv
draft_translation: And those who stood by said, Do you revile God's high priest?
ukjv_translation: And they that stood by said, Revile you God's high priest?

greek_text: εφη τε ο παυλος ουκ ηδειν αδελφοι οτι εστιν αρχιερευς γεγραπται γαρ αρχοντα του λαου σου ουκ ερεις κακως
transliteration: efh te o paulov ouk hdein adelfoi oti estin arciereuv gegraptai gar arconta tou laou sou ouk ereiv kakwv
draft_translation: Then Paul said, I did not know, brothers, that he is the high priest: for it is written, You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people.
ukjv_translation: Then said Paul, I know not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people.

greek_text: γνους δε ο παυλος οτι το εν μερος εστιν σαδδουκαιων το δε ετερον φαρισαιων εκραξεν εν τω συνεδριω ανδρες αδελφοι εγω φαρισαιος ειμι υιος φαρισαιου περι ελπιδος και αναστασεως νεκρων εγω κρινομαι
transliteration: gnouv de o paulov oti to en merov estin saddoukaiwn to de eteron farisaiwn ekraxen en tw sunedriw andrev adelfoi egw farisaiov eimi uiov farisaiou peri elpidov kai anastasewv nekrwn egw krinomai
draft_translation: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged.
ukjv_translation: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

greek_text: τουτο δε αυτου λαλησαντος εγενετο στασις των φαρισαιων και των σαδδουκαιων και εσχισθη το πληθος
transliteration: touto de autou lalhsantov egeneto stasiv twn farisaiwn kai twn saddoukaiwn kai escisyh to plhyov
draft_translation: And when he had so said, there arose a division between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
ukjv_translation: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

greek_text: σαδδουκαιοι μεν γαρ λεγουσιν μη ειναι αναστασιν μηδε αγγελον μητε πνευμα φαρισαιοι δε ομολογουσιν τα αμφοτερα
transliteration: saddoukaioi men gar legousin mh einai anastasin mhde aggelon mhte pneuma farisaioi de omologousin ta amfotera
draft_translation: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
ukjv_translation: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: (o. pneuma) but the Pharisees confess both.
review_notes: removed UKJV inline Strong-style lexical marker

greek_text: εγενετο δε κραυγη μεγαλη και ανασταντες οι γραμματεις του μερους των φαρισαιων διεμαχοντο λεγοντες ουδεν κακον ευρισκομεν εν τω ανθρωπω τουτω ει δε πνευμα ελαλησεν αυτω η αγγελος μη θεομαχωμεν
transliteration: egeneto de kraugh megalh kai anastantev oi grammateiv tou merouv twn farisaiwn diemaconto legontev ouden kakon euriskomen en tw anyrwpw toutw ei de pneuma elalhsen autw h aggelov mh yeomacwmen
draft_translation: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and argued, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
ukjv_translation: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit (o. pneuma) or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

greek_text: πολλης δε γενομενης στασεως ευλαβηθεις ο χιλιαρχος μη διασπασθη ο παυλος υπ αυτων εκελευσεν το στρατευμα καταβαν αρπασαι αυτον εκ μεσου αυτων αγειν τε εις την παρεμβολην
transliteration: pollhv de genomenhv stasewv eulabhyeiv o ciliarcov mh diaspasyh o paulov up autwn ekeleusen to strateuma kataban arpasai auton ek mesou autwn agein te eiv thn parembolhn
draft_translation: And when there arose a great division, the commander, fearing lest Paul should be torn apart by them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the barracks.
ukjv_translation: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.

greek_text: τη δε επιουση νυκτι επιστας αυτω ο κυριος ειπεν θαρσει παυλε ως γαρ διεμαρτυρω τα περι εμου εις ιερουσαλημ ουτως σε δει και εις ρωμην μαρτυρησαι
transliteration: th de epioush nukti epistav autw o kuriov eipen yarsei paule wv gar diemarturw ta peri emou eiv ierousalhm outwv se dei kai eiv rwmhn marturhsai
draft_translation: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Take courage, Paul: for as you have testified of me in Jerusalem, so you must bear witness also at Rome.
ukjv_translation: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as you have testified of me in Jerusalem, so must you bear witness also at Rome.

greek_text: γενομενης δε ημερας ποιησαντες τινες των ιουδαιων συστροφην ανεθεματισαν εαυτους λεγοντες μητε φαγειν μητε πιειν εως ου αποκτεινωσιν τον παυλον
transliteration: genomenhv de hmerav poihsantev tinev twn ioudaiwn sustrofhn aneyematisan eautouv legontev mhte fagein mhte piein ewv ou apokteinwsin ton paulon
draft_translation: And when it was day, certain of the Jews formed a conspiracy, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
ukjv_translation: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

greek_text: ησαν δε πλειους τεσσαρακοντα οι ταυτην την συνωμοσιαν πεποιηκοτες
transliteration: hsan de pleiouv tessarakonta oi tauthn thn sunwmosian pepoihkotev
draft_translation: And they were more than forty who had made this conspiracy.
ukjv_translation: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

greek_text: οιτινες προσελθοντες τοις αρχιερευσιν και τοις πρεσβυτεροις ειπον αναθεματι ανεθεματισαμεν εαυτους μηδενος γευσασθαι εως ου αποκτεινωμεν τον παυλον
transliteration: oitinev proselyontev toiv arciereusin kai toiv presbuteroiv eipon anayemati aneyematisamen eautouv mhdenov geusasyai ewv ou apokteinwmen ton paulon
draft_translation: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
ukjv_translation: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

greek_text: νυν ουν υμεις εμφανισατε τω χιλιαρχω συν τω συνεδριω οπως αυριον αυτον καταγαγη προς υμας ως μελλοντας διαγινωσκειν ακριβεστερον τα περι αυτου ημεις δε προ του εγγισαι αυτον ετοιμοι εσμεν του ανελειν αυτον
transliteration: nun oun umeiv emfanisate tw ciliarcw sun tw sunedriw opwv aurion auton katagagh prov umav wv mellontav diaginwskein akribesteron ta peri autou hmeiv de pro tou eggisai auton etoimoi esmen tou anelein auton
draft_translation: Now therefore you with the council notify the commander that he bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you would examine his case more accurately: and we, before he comes near, are ready to kill him.
ukjv_translation: Now therefore all of you with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you tomorrow, as though all of you would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, before even he comes near, are ready to kill him.

greek_text: ακουσας δε ο υιος της αδελφης παυλου την ενεδραν παραγενομενος και εισελθων εις την παρεμβολην απηγγειλεν τω παυλω
transliteration: akousav de o uiov thv adelfhv paulou thn enedran paragenomenov kai eiselywn eiv thn parembolhn aphggeilen tw paulw
draft_translation: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their ambush, he went and entered into the barracks, and told Paul.
ukjv_translation: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

greek_text: προσκαλεσαμενος δε ο παυλος ενα των εκατονταρχων εφη τον νεανιαν τουτον απαγαγε προς τον χιλιαρχον εχει γαρ τι απαγγειλαι αυτω
transliteration: proskalesamenov de o paulov ena twn ekatontarcwn efh ton neanian touton apagage prov ton ciliarcon ecei gar ti apaggeilai autw
draft_translation: Then Paul called one of the centurions to him, and said, Bring this young man to the commander: for he has a certain thing to tell him.
ukjv_translation: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he has a certain thing to tell him.

greek_text: ο μεν ουν παραλαβων αυτον ηγαγεν προς τον χιλιαρχον και φησιν ο δεσμιος παυλος προσκαλεσαμενος με ηρωτησεν τουτον τον νεανιαν αγαγειν προς σε εχοντα τι λαλησαι σοι
transliteration: o men oun paralabwn auton hgagen prov ton ciliarcon kai fhsin o desmiov paulov proskalesamenov me hrwthsen touton ton neanian agagein prov se econta ti lalhsai soi
draft_translation: So he took him, and brought him to the commander, and said, Paul the prisoner called me to him, and asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to say to you.
ukjv_translation: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto you, who has something to say unto you.

greek_text: επιλαβομενος δε της χειρος αυτου ο χιλιαρχος και αναχωρησας κατ ιδιαν επυνθανετο τι εστιν ο εχεις απαγγειλαι μοι
transliteration: epilabomenov de thv ceirov autou o ciliarcov kai anacwrhsav kat idian epunyaneto ti estin o eceiv apaggeilai moi
draft_translation: Then the commander took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that you have to tell me?
ukjv_translation: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that you have to tell me?

greek_text: ειπεν δε οτι οι ιουδαιοι συνεθεντο του ερωτησαι σε οπως αυριον εις το συνεδριον καταγαγης τον παυλον ως μελλοντες τι ακριβεστερον πυνθανεσθαι περι αυτου
transliteration: eipen de oti oi ioudaioi suneyento tou erwthsai se opwv aurion eiv to sunedrion katagaghv ton paulon wv mellontev ti akribesteron punyanesyai peri autou
draft_translation: And he said, The Jews have agreed to ask you that you would bring down Paul tomorrow into the council, as though they would inquire somewhat of him more accurately.
ukjv_translation: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire you that you would bring down Paul tomorrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

greek_text: συ ουν μη πεισθης αυτοις ενεδρευουσιν γαρ αυτον εξ αυτων ανδρες πλειους τεσσαρακοντα οιτινες ανεθεματισαν εαυτους μητε φαγειν μητε πιειν εως ου ανελωσιν αυτον και νυν ετοιμοι εισιν προσδεχομενοι την απο σου επαγγελιαν
transliteration: su oun mh peisyhv autoiv enedreuousin gar auton ex autwn andrev pleiouv tessarakonta oitinev aneyematisan eautouv mhte fagein mhte piein ewv ou anelwsin auton kai nun etoimoi eisin prosdecomenoi thn apo sou epaggelian
draft_translation: But do not yield to them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, who have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from you.
ukjv_translation: But do not you yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from you.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized do-not-you imperative; modernized personal which as who

greek_text: ο μεν ουν χιλιαρχος απελυσεν τον νεανιαν παραγγειλας μηδενι εκλαλησαι οτι ταυτα ενεφανισας προς με
transliteration: o men oun ciliarcov apelusen ton neanian paraggeilav mhdeni eklalhsai oti tauta enefanisav prov me
draft_translation: So the commander then let the young man depart, and charged him, Tell no one that you have disclosed these things to me.
ukjv_translation: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See you tell no man that you have showed these things to me.

greek_text: και προσκαλεσαμενος δυο τινας των εκατονταρχων ειπεν ετοιμασατε στρατιωτας διακοσιους οπως πορευθωσιν εως καισαρειας και ιππεις εβδομηκοντα και δεξιολαβους διακοσιους απο τριτης ωρας της νυκτος
transliteration: kai proskalesamenov duo tinav twn ekatontarcwn eipen etoimasate stratiwtav diakosiouv opwv poreuywsin ewv kaisareiav kai ippeiv ebdomhkonta kai dexiolabouv diakosiouv apo trithv wrav thv nuktov
draft_translation: And he called to him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, at the third hour of the night;
ukjv_translation: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

greek_text: κτηνη τε παραστησαι ινα επιβιβασαντες τον παυλον διασωσωσιν προς φηλικα τον ηγεμονα
transliteration: kthnh te parasthsai ina epibibasantev ton paulon diaswswsin prov fhlika ton hgemona
draft_translation: And provide mounts, that they may set Paul on them, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
ukjv_translation: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

greek_text: γραψας επιστολην περιεχουσαν τον τυπον τουτον
transliteration: graqav epistolhn periecousan ton tupon touton
draft_translation: And he wrote a letter in this form:
ukjv_translation: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

greek_text: κλαυδιος λυσιας τω κρατιστω ηγεμονι φηλικι χαιρειν
transliteration: klaudiov lusiav tw kratistw hgemoni fhliki cairein
draft_translation: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix sends greeting.
ukjv_translation: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sends greeting.

greek_text: τον ανδρα τουτον συλληφθεντα υπο των ιουδαιων και μελλοντα αναιρεισθαι υπ αυτων επιστας συν τω στρατευματι εξειλομην αυτον μαθων οτι ρωμαιος εστιν
transliteration: ton andra touton sullhfyenta upo twn ioudaiwn kai mellonta anaireisyai up autwn epistav sun tw strateumati exeilomhn auton maywn oti rwmaiov estin
draft_translation: This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them: then I came with the troops, and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
ukjv_translation: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

greek_text: βουλομενος δε γνωναι την αιτιαν δι ην ενεκαλουν αυτω κατηγαγον αυτον εις το συνεδριον αυτων
transliteration: boulomenov de gnwnai thn aitian di hn enekaloun autw kathgagon auton eiv to sunedrion autwn
draft_translation: And wishing to know the cause for which they accused him, I brought him down into their council:
ukjv_translation: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

greek_text: ον ευρον εγκαλουμενον περι ζητηματων του νομου αυτων μηδεν δε αξιον θανατου η δεσμων εγκλημα εχοντα
