transliteration: on euron egkaloumenon peri zhthmatwn tou nomou autwn mhden de axion yanatou h desmwn egklhma econta
draft_translation: Whom I found to be accused concerning questions of their law, but to have no charge laid against him worthy of death or of bonds.
ukjv_translation: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

greek_text: μηνυθεισης δε μοι επιβουλης εις τον ανδρα μελλειν εσεσθαι υπο των ιουδαιων εξαυτης επεμψα προς σε παραγγειλας και τοις κατηγοροις λεγειν τα προς αυτον επι σου ερρωσο
transliteration: mhnuyeishv de moi epiboulhv eiv ton andra mellein esesyai upo twn ioudaiwn exauthv epemqa prov se paraggeilav kai toiv kathgoroiv legein ta prov auton epi sou errwso
draft_translation: And when it was told me that a plot against the man was about to be made by the Jews, I sent him immediately to you, and commanded his accusers also to say before you what they had against him. Farewell.
ukjv_translation: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent immediately to you, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before you what they had against him. Farewell.

greek_text: οι μεν ουν στρατιωται κατα το διατεταγμενον αυτοις αναλαβοντες τον παυλον ηγαγον δια της νυκτος εις την αντιπατριδα
transliteration: oi men oun stratiwtai kata to diatetagmenon autoiv analabontev ton paulon hgagon dia thv nuktov eiv thn antipatrida
draft_translation: Then the soldiers, according to what was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
ukjv_translation: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

greek_text: τη δε επαυριον εασαντες τους ιππεις πορευεσθαι συν αυτω υπεστρεψαν εις την παρεμβολην
transliteration: th de epaurion easantev touv ippeiv poreuesyai sun autw upestreqan eiv thn parembolhn
draft_translation: On the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks:
ukjv_translation: On the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

greek_text: οιτινες εισελθοντες εις την καισαρειαν και αναδοντες την επιστολην τω ηγεμονι παρεστησαν και τον παυλον αυτω
transliteration: oitinev eiselyontev eiv thn kaisareian kai anadontev thn epistolhn tw hgemoni paresthsan kai ton paulon autw
draft_translation: Who, when they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
ukjv_translation: Who, when they came to Caesarea and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

greek_text: αναγνους δε ο ηγεμων και επερωτησας εκ ποιας επαρχιας εστιν και πυθομενος οτι απο κιλικιας
transliteration: anagnouv de o hgemwn kai eperwthsav ek poiav eparciav estin kai puyomenov oti apo kilikiav
draft_translation: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked from what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
ukjv_translation: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;

greek_text: διακουσομαι σου εφη οταν και οι κατηγοροι σου παραγενωνται εκελευσεν τε αυτον εν τω πραιτωριω του ηρωδου φυλασσεσθαι
transliteration: diakousomai sou efh otan kai oi kathgoroi sou paragenwntai ekeleusen te auton en tw praitwriw tou hrwdou fulassesyai
draft_translation: I will hear you fully, said he, when your accusers have also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's Praetorium.
ukjv_translation: I will hear you, said he, when yours accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.

greek_text: μετα δε πεντε ημερας κατεβη ο αρχιερευς ανανιας μετα των πρεσβυτερων και ρητορος τερτυλλου τινος οιτινες ενεφανισαν τω ηγεμονι κατα του παυλου
transliteration: meta de pente hmerav katebh o arciereuv ananiav meta twn presbuterwn kai rhtorov tertullou tinov oitinev enefanisan tw hgemoni kata tou paulou
draft_translation: And after five days Ananias the high priest came down with the elders, and with a certain attorney named Tertullus, who laid information before the governor against Paul.
ukjv_translation: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

greek_text: κληθεντος δε αυτου ηρξατο κατηγορειν ο τερτυλλος λεγων πολλης ειρηνης τυγχανοντες δια σου και κατορθωματων γινομενων τω εθνει τουτω δια της σης προνοιας
transliteration: klhyentov de autou hrxato kathgorein o tertullov legwn pollhv eirhnhv tugcanontev dia sou kai katorywmatwn ginomenwn tw eynei toutw dia thv shv pronoiav
draft_translation: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that reforms are done for this nation by your foresight,
ukjv_translation: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by you we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by your providence,

greek_text: παντη τε και πανταχου αποδεχομεθα κρατιστε φηλιξ μετα πασης ευχαριστιας
transliteration: panth te kai pantacou apodecomeya kratiste fhlix meta pashv eucaristiav
draft_translation: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
ukjv_translation: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
review_notes: UKJV seed retained; needs focused Greek review

greek_text: ινα δε μη επι πλειον σε εγκοπτω παρακαλω ακουσαι σε ημων συντομως τη ση επιεικεια
transliteration: ina de mh epi pleion se egkoptw parakalw akousai se hmwn suntomwv th sh epieikeia
draft_translation: Notwithstanding, that I may not be wearisome anymore to you, I ask you that you would hear us of your clemency a few words.
ukjv_translation: Notwithstanding, that I be not wearisome anymore unto you, I pray you that you would hear us of your clemency a few words.
review_notes: modernized I-pray-you wording; modernized archaic directional unto; modernized be-not clause

greek_text: ευροντες γαρ τον ανδρα τουτον λοιμον και κινουντα στασιν πασιν τοις ιουδαιοις τοις κατα την οικουμενην πρωτοστατην τε της των ναζωραιων αιρεσεως
transliteration: eurontev gar ton andra touton loimon kai kinounta stasin pasin toiv ioudaioiv toiv kata thn oikoumenhn prwtostathn te thv twn nazwraiwn airesewv
draft_translation: For we have found this man a plague, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
ukjv_translation: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

greek_text: ος και το ιερον επειρασεν βεβηλωσαι ον και εκρατησαμεν και κατα τον ημετερον νομον ηθελησαμεν κρινειν
transliteration: ov kai to ieron epeirasen bebhlwsai on kai ekrathsamen kai kata ton hmeteron nomon hyelhsamen krinein
draft_translation: Who also attempted to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
ukjv_translation: Who also has gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.

greek_text: παρελθων δε λυσιας ο χιλιαρχος μετα πολλης βιας εκ των χειρων ημων απηγαγεν
transliteration: parelywn de lusiav o ciliarcov meta pollhv biav ek twn ceirwn hmwn aphgagen
draft_translation: But the commander Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,
ukjv_translation: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

greek_text: κελευσας τους κατηγορους αυτου ερχεσθαι επι σε παρ ου δυνηση αυτος ανακρινας περι παντων τουτων επιγνωναι ων ημεις κατηγορουμεν αυτου
transliteration: keleusav touv kathgorouv autou ercesyai epi se par ou dunhsh autov anakrinav peri pantwn toutwn epignwnai wn hmeiv kathgoroumen autou
draft_translation: Commanding his accusers to come to you: by examining him yourself you may learn all these things, of which we accuse him.
ukjv_translation: Commanding his accusers to come unto you: by examining of whom yourself may take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.

greek_text: συνεθεντο δε και οι ιουδαιοι φασκοντες ταυτα ουτως εχειν
transliteration: suneyento de kai oi ioudaioi faskontev tauta outwv ecein
draft_translation: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
ukjv_translation: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

greek_text: απεκριθη δε ο παυλος νευσαντος αυτω του ηγεμονος λεγειν εκ πολλων ετων οντα σε κριτην τω εθνει τουτω επισταμενος ευθυμοτερον τα περι εμαυτου απολογουμαι
transliteration: apekriyh de o paulov neusantov autw tou hgemonov legein ek pollwn etwn onta se krithn tw eynei toutw epistamenov euyumoteron ta peri emautou apologoumai
draft_translation: Then Paul, after the governor had beckoned to him to speak, answered, Since I know that you have been for many years a judge to this nation, I more cheerfully make my defense:
ukjv_translation: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that you have been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

greek_text: δυναμενου σου γνωναι οτι ου πλειους εισιν μοι ημεραι η δεκαδυο αφ ης ανεβην προσκυνησων εν ιερουσαλημ
transliteration: dunamenou sou gnwnai oti ou pleiouv eisin moi hmerai h dekaduo af hv anebhn proskunhswn en ierousalhm
draft_translation: Because you may understand, that there are no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem in order to worship.
ukjv_translation: Because that you may understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem in order to worship.

greek_text: και ουτε εν τω ιερω ευρον με προς τινα διαλεγομενον η επισυστασιν ποιουντα οχλου ουτε εν ταις συναγωγαις ουτε κατα την πολιν
transliteration: kai oute en tw ierw euron me prov tina dialegomenon h episustasin poiounta oclou oute en taiv sunagwgaiv oute kata thn polin
draft_translation: And they neither found me in the temple arguing with anyone, nor stirring up a crowd, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
ukjv_translation: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

greek_text: ουτε παραστησαι δυνανται περι ων νυν κατηγορουσιν μου
transliteration: oute parasthsai dunantai peri wn nun kathgorousin mou
draft_translation: Neither can they prove the things of which they now accuse me.
ukjv_translation: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.

greek_text: ομολογω δε τουτο σοι οτι κατα την οδον ην λεγουσιν αιρεσιν ουτως λατρευω τω πατρωω θεω πιστευων πασιν τοις κατα τον νομον και τοις προφηταις γεγραμμενοις
transliteration: omologw de touto soi oti kata thn odon hn legousin airesin outwv latreuw tw patrww yew pisteuwn pasin toiv kata ton nomon kai toiv profhtaiv gegrammenoiv
draft_translation: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, so I worship the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
ukjv_translation: But this I confess unto you, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

greek_text: ελπιδα εχων εις τον θεον ην και αυτοι ουτοι προσδεχονται αναστασιν μελλειν εσεσθαι νεκρων δικαιων τε και αδικων
transliteration: elpida ecwn eiv ton yeon hn kai autoi outoi prosdecontai anastasin mellein esesyai nekrwn dikaiwn te kai adikwn
draft_translation: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also accept, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
ukjv_translation: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

greek_text: εν τουτω δε αυτος ασκω απροσκοπον συνειδησιν εχειν προς τον θεον και τους ανθρωπους δια παντος
transliteration: en toutw de autov askw aproskopon suneidhsin ecein prov ton yeon kai touv anyrwpouv dia pantov
draft_translation: And in this I also strive, to have always a conscience without offense toward God, and toward men.
ukjv_translation: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void to offence toward God, and toward men.

greek_text: δι ετων δε πλειονων παρεγενομην ελεημοσυνας ποιησων εις το εθνος μου και προσφορας
transliteration: di etwn de pleionwn paregenomhn elehmosunav poihswn eiv to eynov mou kai prosforav
draft_translation: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
ukjv_translation: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

greek_text: εν οις ευρον με ηγνισμενον εν τω ιερω ου μετα οχλου ουδε μετα θορυβου τινες απο της ασιας ιουδαιοι
transliteration: en oiv euron me hgnismenon en tw ierw ou meta oclou oude meta yorubou tinev apo thv asiav ioudaioi
draft_translation: In which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with crowd, nor with tumult.
ukjv_translation: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

greek_text: ους εδει επι σου παρειναι και κατηγορειν ει τι εχοιεν προς με
transliteration: ouv edei epi sou pareinai kai kathgorein ei ti ecoien prov me
draft_translation: Who ought to have been here before you, and to accuse me, if they had anything against me.
ukjv_translation: Who ought to have been here before you, and object, if they had ought against me.

greek_text: η αυτοι ουτοι ειπατωσαν ει τι ευρον εν εμοι αδικημα σταντος μου επι του συνεδριου
transliteration: h autoi outoi eipatwsan ei ti euron en emoi adikhma stantov mou epi tou sunedriou
draft_translation: Or else let these same here say, if they found any wrongdoing in me, while I stood before the council,
ukjv_translation: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

greek_text: η περι μιας ταυτης φωνης ης εκραξα εστως εν αυτοις οτι περι αναστασεως νεκρων εγω κρινομαι σημερον υφ υμων
transliteration: h peri miav tauthv fwnhv hv ekraxa estwv en autoiv oti peri anastasewv nekrwn egw krinomai shmeron uf umwn
draft_translation: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged by you this day.
ukjv_translation: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

greek_text: ακουσας δε ταυτα ο φηλιξ ανεβαλετο αυτους ακριβεστερον ειδως τα περι της οδου ειπων οταν λυσιας ο χιλιαρχος καταβη διαγνωσομαι τα καθ υμας
transliteration: akousav de tauta o fhlix anebaleto autouv akribesteron eidwv ta peri thv odou eipwn otan lusiav o ciliarcov katabh diagnwsomai ta kay umav
draft_translation: And when Felix heard these things, having more accurate knowledge of the Way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the commander shall come down, I will determine your matter.
ukjv_translation: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

greek_text: διαταξαμενος τε τω εκατονταρχη τηρεισθαι τον παυλον εχειν τε ανεσιν και μηδενα κωλυειν των ιδιων αυτου υπηρετειν η προσερχεσθαι αυτω
transliteration: diataxamenov te tw ekatontarch threisyai ton paulon ecein te anesin kai mhdena kwluein twn idiwn autou uphretein h prosercesyai autw
draft_translation: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his own to minister or come to him.
ukjv_translation: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

greek_text: μετα δε ημερας τινας παραγενομενος ο φηλιξ συν δρουσιλλη τη γυναικι αυτου ουση ιουδαια μετεπεμψατο τον παυλον και ηκουσεν αυτου περι της εις χριστον πιστεως
transliteration: meta de hmerav tinav paragenomenov o fhlix sun drousillh th gunaiki autou oush ioudaia metepemqato ton paulon kai hkousen autou peri thv eiv criston pistewv
draft_translation: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
ukjv_translation: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

greek_text: διαλεγομενου δε αυτου περι δικαιοσυνης και εγκρατειας και του κριματος του μελλοντος εσεσθαι εμφοβος γενομενος ο φηλιξ απεκριθη το νυν εχον πορευου καιρον δε μεταλαβων μετακαλεσομαι σε
transliteration: dialegomenou de autou peri dikaiosunhv kai egkrateiav kai tou krimatov tou mellontov esesyai emfobov genomenov o fhlix apekriyh to nun econ poreuou kairon de metalabwn metakalesomai se
draft_translation: And as he reasoned of righteousness, self-control, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go your way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for you.
ukjv_translation: And as he reasoned of righteousness, wilful restrain, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go your way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for you.

greek_text: αμα δε και ελπιζων οτι χρηματα δοθησεται αυτω υπο του παυλου οπως λυση αυτον διο και πυκνοτερον αυτον μεταπεμπομενος ωμιλει αυτω
transliteration: ama de kai elpizwn oti crhmata doyhsetai autw upo tou paulou opwv lush auton dio kai puknoteron auton metapempomenov wmilei autw
draft_translation: He also hoped that money would be given him by Paul, that he might release him: therefore he sent for him more often, and conversed with him.
ukjv_translation: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

greek_text: διετιας δε πληρωθεισης ελαβεν διαδοχον ο φηλιξ πορκιον φηστον θελων τε χαριτας καταθεσθαι τοις ιουδαιοις ο φηλιξ κατελιπεν τον παυλον δεδεμενον
transliteration: dietiav de plhrwyeishv elaben diadocon o fhlix porkion fhston yelwn te caritav katayesyai toiv ioudaioiv o fhlix katelipen ton paulon dedemenon
draft_translation: But after two years Porcius Festus came as Felix's successor: and Felix, willing to grant the Jews a favor, left Paul bound.
ukjv_translation: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to show the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.

greek_text: φηστος ουν επιβας τη επαρχια μετα τρεις ημερας ανεβη εις ιεροσολυμα απο καισαρειας
transliteration: fhstov oun epibav th eparcia meta treiv hmerav anebh eiv ierosoluma apo kaisareiav
draft_translation: Now when Festus had entered the province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
ukjv_translation: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

greek_text: ενεφανισαν δε αυτω ο αρχιερευς και οι πρωτοι των ιουδαιων κατα του παυλου και παρεκαλουν αυτον
transliteration: enefanisan de autw o arciereuv kai oi prwtoi twn ioudaiwn kata tou paulou kai parekaloun auton
draft_translation: Then the high priest and the chief men of the Jews laid information before him against Paul, and begged him,
ukjv_translation: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,

greek_text: αιτουμενοι χαριν κατ αυτου οπως μεταπεμψηται αυτον εις ιερουσαλημ ενεδραν ποιουντες ανελειν αυτον κατα την οδον
transliteration: aitoumenoi carin kat autou opwv metapemqhtai auton eiv ierousalhm enedran poiountev anelein auton kata thn odon
draft_translation: And desired favor against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
ukjv_translation: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

greek_text: ο μεν ουν φηστος απεκριθη τηρεισθαι τον παυλον εν καισαρεια εαυτον δε μελλειν εν ταχει εκπορευεσθαι
transliteration: o men oun fhstov apekriyh threisyai ton paulon en kaisareia eauton de mellein en tacei ekporeuesyai
draft_translation: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart there shortly.
ukjv_translation: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.

greek_text: οι ουν δυνατοι εν υμιν φησιν συγκαταβαντες ει τι εστιν ατοπον εν τω ανδρι τουτω κατηγορειτωσαν αυτου
transliteration: oi oun dunatoi en umin fhsin sugkatabantev ei ti estin atopon en tw andri toutw kathgoreitwsan autou
draft_translation: Let them therefore, said he, who are able among you, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there is any wrongdoing in him.
ukjv_translation: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

greek_text: διατριψας δε εν αυτοις ημερας πλειους η δεκα καταβας εις καισαρειαν τη επαυριον καθισας επι του βηματος εκελευσεν τον παυλον αχθηναι
transliteration: diatriqav de en autoiv hmerav pleiouv h deka katabav eiv kaisareian th epaurion kayisav epi tou bhmatov ekeleusen ton paulon acyhnai
draft_translation: And when he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
ukjv_translation: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

greek_text: παραγενομενου δε αυτου περιεστησαν οι απο ιεροσολυμων καταβεβηκοτες ιουδαιοι πολλα και βαρεα αιτιαματα φεροντες κατα του παυλου α ουκ ισχυον αποδειξαι
transliteration: paragenomenou de autou periesthsan oi apo ierosolumwn katabebhkotev ioudaioi polla kai barea aitiamata ferontev kata tou paulou a ouk iscuon apodeixai
draft_translation: And when he had come, the Jews who came down from Jerusalem stood around, bringing many and grievous charges against Paul, which they could not prove.
ukjv_translation: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

greek_text: απολογουμενου αυτου οτι ουτε εις τον νομον των ιουδαιων ουτε εις το ιερον ουτε εις καισαρα τι ημαρτον
transliteration: apologoumenou autou oti oute eiv ton nomon twn ioudaiwn oute eiv to ieron oute eiv kaisara ti hmarton
draft_translation: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.
ukjv_translation: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.

greek_text: ο φηστος δε τοις ιουδαιοις θελων χαριν καταθεσθαι αποκριθεις τω παυλω ειπεν θελεις εις ιεροσολυμα αναβας εκει περι τουτων κρινεσθαι επ εμου
transliteration: o fhstov de toiv ioudaioiv yelwn carin katayesyai apokriyeiv tw paulw eipen yeleiv eiv ierosoluma anabav ekei peri toutwn krinesyai ep emou
draft_translation: But Festus, willing to grant the Jews a favor, answered Paul, and said, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
ukjv_translation: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?

greek_text: ειπεν δε ο παυλος επι του βηματος καισαρος εστως ειμι ου με δει κρινεσθαι ιουδαιους ουδεν ηδικησα ως και συ καλλιον επιγινωσκεις
transliteration: eipen de o paulov epi tou bhmatov kaisarov estwv eimi ou me dei krinesyai ioudaiouv ouden hdikhsa wv kai su kallion epiginwskeiv
draft_translation: Then Paul said, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews I have done no wrong, as you very well know.
ukjv_translation: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as you very well know.

greek_text: ει μεν γαρ αδικω και αξιον θανατου πεπραχα τι ου παραιτουμαι το αποθανειν ει δε ουδεν εστιν ων ουτοι κατηγορουσιν μου ουδεις με δυναται αυτοις χαρισασθαι καισαρα επικαλουμαι
transliteration: ei men gar adikw kai axion yanatou pepraca ti ou paraitoumai to apoyanein ei de ouden estin wn outoi kathgorousin mou oudeiv me dunatai autoiv carisasyai kaisara epikaloumai
draft_translation: For if I am a wrongdoer, or have committed anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die: but if there is none of these things of which these accuse me, no one may hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar.
ukjv_translation: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.

greek_text: τοτε ο φηστος συλλαλησας μετα του συμβουλιου απεκριθη καισαρα επικεκλησαι επι καισαρα πορευση
transliteration: tote o fhstov sullalhsav meta tou sumbouliou apekriyh kaisara epikeklhsai epi kaisara poreush
draft_translation: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Have you appealed to Caesar? to Caesar shall you go.
ukjv_translation: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Have you appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shall you go.

greek_text: ημερων δε διαγενομενων τινων αγριππας ο βασιλευς και βερνικη κατηντησαν εις καισαρειαν ασπασομενοι τον φηστον
transliteration: hmerwn de diagenomenwn tinwn agrippav o basileuv kai bernikh kathnthsan eiv kaisareian aspasomenoi ton fhston
draft_translation: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to salute Festus.
ukjv_translation: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.

greek_text: ως δε πλειους ημερας διετριβον εκει ο φηστος τω βασιλει ανεθετο τα κατα τον παυλον λεγων ανηρ τις εστιν καταλελειμμενος υπο φηλικος δεσμιος
transliteration: wv de pleiouv hmerav dietribon ekei o fhstov tw basilei aneyeto ta kata ton paulon legwn anhr tiv estin kataleleimmenov upo fhlikov desmiov
draft_translation: And when they had been there many days, Festus laid Paul's case before the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
ukjv_translation: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

greek_text: περι ου γενομενου μου εις ιεροσολυμα ενεφανισαν οι αρχιερεις και οι πρεσβυτεροι των ιουδαιων αιτουμενοι κατ αυτου δικην
transliteration: peri ou genomenou mou eiv ierosoluma enefanisan oi arciereiv kai oi presbuteroi twn ioudaiwn aitoumenoi kat autou dikhn
draft_translation: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews laid information before me, asking for judgment against him.
ukjv_translation: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.

greek_text: προς ους απεκριθην οτι ουκ εστιν εθος ρωμαιοις χαριζεσθαι τινα ανθρωπον εις απωλειαν πριν η ο κατηγορουμενος κατα προσωπον εχοι τους κατηγορους τοπον τε απολογιας λαβοι περι του εγκληματος
transliteration: prov ouv apekriyhn oti ouk estin eyov rwmaioiv carizesyai tina anyrwpon eiv apwleian prin h o kathgoroumenov kata proswpon ecoi touv kathgorouv topon te apologiav laboi peri tou egklhmatov
draft_translation: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver anyone to die, before that the one who is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
ukjv_translation: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
review_notes: modernized any-man idiom; modernized he-which relative

greek_text: συνελθοντων ουν αυτων ενθαδε αναβολην μηδεμιαν ποιησαμενος τη εξης καθισας επι του βηματος εκελευσα αχθηναι τον ανδρα
transliteration: sunelyontwn oun autwn enyade anabolhn mhdemian poihsamenov th exhv kayisav epi tou bhmatov ekeleusa acyhnai ton andra
draft_translation: Therefore, when they had come here, without any delay on the next day I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought.
ukjv_translation: Therefore, when they were come here, without any delay on the next day I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

greek_text: περι ου σταθεντες οι κατηγοροι ουδεμιαν αιτιαν επεφερον ων υπενοουν εγω
transliteration: peri ou stayentev oi kathgoroi oudemian aitian epeferon wn upenooun egw
draft_translation: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation of such things as I supposed:
ukjv_translation: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:

greek_text: ζητηματα δε τινα περι της ιδιας δεισιδαιμονιας ειχον προς αυτον και περι τινος ιησου τεθνηκοτος ον εφασκεν ο παυλος ζην
transliteration: zhthmata de tina peri thv idiav deisidaimoniav eicon prov auton kai peri tinov ihsou teynhkotov on efasken o paulov zhn
draft_translation: But had certain questions against him of their own religion, and of one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
ukjv_translation: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

greek_text: απορουμενος δε εγω εις την περι τουτου ζητησιν ελεγον ει βουλοιτο πορευεσθαι εις ιερουσαλημ κακει κρινεσθαι περι τουτων
transliteration: aporoumenov de egw eiv thn peri toutou zhthsin elegon ei bouloito poreuesyai eiv ierousalhm kakei krinesyai peri toutwn
draft_translation: And because I was perplexed about this inquiry, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
ukjv_translation: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

greek_text: του δε παυλου επικαλεσαμενου τηρηθηναι αυτον εις την του σεβαστου διαγνωσιν εκελευσα τηρεισθαι αυτον εως ου πεμψω αυτον προς καισαρα
transliteration: tou de paulou epikalesamenou thrhyhnai auton eiv thn tou sebastou diagnwsin ekeleusa threisyai auton ewv ou pemqw auton prov kaisara
draft_translation: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved to the decision of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
ukjv_translation: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.

greek_text: αγριππας δε προς τον φηστον εφη εβουλομην και αυτος του ανθρωπου ακουσαι ο δε αυριον φησιν ακουση αυτου
transliteration: agrippav de prov ton fhston efh eboulomhn kai autov tou anyrwpou akousai o de aurion fhsin akoush autou
draft_translation: Then Agrippa said to Festus, I would also hear the man myself. Tomorrow, said he, you shall hear him.
ukjv_translation: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. Tomorrow, said he, you shall hear him.

greek_text: τη ουν επαυριον ελθοντος του αγριππα και της βερνικης μετα πολλης φαντασιας και εισελθοντων εις το ακροατηριον συν τε τοις χιλιαρχοις και ανδρασιν τοις κατ εξοχην ουσιν της πολεως και κελευσαντος του φηστου ηχθη ο παυλος
transliteration: th oun epaurion elyontov tou agrippa kai thv bernikhv meta pollhv fantasiav kai eiselyontwn eiv to akroathrion sun te toiv ciliarcoiv kai andrasin toiv kat exochn ousin thv polewv kai keleusantov tou fhstou hcyh o paulov
draft_translation: And on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and had entered into the audience hall, with the commanders and principal men of the city, at Festus' command Paul was brought.
ukjv_translation: And on the next day, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth.

greek_text: και φησιν ο φηστος αγριππα βασιλευ και παντες οι συμπαροντες ημιν ανδρες θεωρειτε τουτον περι ου παν το πληθος των ιουδαιων ενετυχον μοι εν τε ιεροσολυμοις και ενθαδε επιβοωντες μη δειν ζην αυτον μηκετι
transliteration: kai fhsin o fhstov agrippa basileu kai pantev oi sumparontev hmin andrev yewreite touton peri ou pan to plhyov twn ioudaiwn enetucon moi en te ierosolumoiv kai enyade epibowntev mh dein zhn auton mhketi
draft_translation: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have petitioned me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
ukjv_translation: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, all of you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

greek_text: εγω δε καταλαβομενος μηδεν αξιον θανατου αυτον πεπραχεναι και αυτου δε τουτου επικαλεσαμενου τον σεβαστον εκρινα πεμπειν αυτον
transliteration: egw de katalabomenov mhden axion yanatou auton pepracenai kai autou de toutou epikalesamenou ton sebaston ekrina pempein auton
draft_translation: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I determined to send him.
ukjv_translation: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

greek_text: περι ου ασφαλες τι γραψαι τω κυριω ουκ εχω διο προηγαγον αυτον εφ υμων και μαλιστα επι σου βασιλευ αγριππα οπως της ανακρισεως γενομενης σχω τι γραψαι
transliteration: peri ou asfalev ti graqai tw kuriw ouk ecw dio prohgagon auton ef umwn kai malista epi sou basileu agrippa opwv thv anakrisewv genomenhv scw ti graqai
draft_translation: Of whom I have no certain thing to write to the emperor. Therefore I have brought him forth before you, and especially before you, O king Agrippa, that, after examination has taken place, I might have something to write.
ukjv_translation: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before you, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

greek_text: αλογον γαρ μοι δοκει πεμποντα δεσμιον μη και τας κατ αυτου αιτιας σημαναι
transliteration: alogon gar moi dokei pemponta desmion mh kai tav kat autou aitiav shmanai
draft_translation: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not also to signify the charges against him.
ukjv_translation: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not likewise to signify the crimes laid against him.

greek_text: αγριππας δε προς τον παυλον εφη επιτρεπεται σοι υπερ σεαυτου λεγειν τοτε ο παυλος απελογειτο εκτεινας την χειρα
transliteration: agrippav de prov ton paulon efh epitrepetai soi uper seautou legein tote o paulov apelogeito ekteinav thn ceira
draft_translation: Then Agrippa said to Paul, You are permitted to speak for yourself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and made his defense:
ukjv_translation: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, You are permitted to speak for yourself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

greek_text: περι παντων ων εγκαλουμαι υπο ιουδαιων βασιλευ αγριππα ηγημαι εμαυτον μακαριον μελλων απολογεισθαι επι σου σημερον
transliteration: peri pantwn wn egkaloumai upo ioudaiwn basileu agrippa hghmai emauton makarion mellwn apologeisyai epi sou shmeron
draft_translation: I consider myself fortunate, king Agrippa, because I shall make my defense this day before you concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews:
ukjv_translation: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before you concerning all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:

greek_text: μαλιστα γνωστην οντα σε ειδως παντων των κατα ιουδαιους εθων τε και ζητηματων διο δεομαι σου μακροθυμως ακουσαι μου
transliteration: malista gnwsthn onta se eidwv pantwn twn kata ioudaiouv eywn te kai zhthmatwn dio deomai sou makroyumwv akousai mou
draft_translation: Especially because I know you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: therefore I ask you to hear me patiently.
ukjv_translation: Especially because I know you to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I plead to you to hear me patiently.

greek_text: την μεν ουν βιωσιν μου την εκ νεοτητος την απ αρχης γενομενην εν τω εθνει μου εν ιεροσολυμοις ισασιν παντες οι ιουδαιοι
transliteration: thn men oun biwsin mou thn ek neothtov thn ap archv genomenhn en tw eynei mou en ierosolumoiv isasin pantev oi ioudaioi
draft_translation: My manner of life from my youth, which was from the beginning among my own nation at Jerusalem, all the Jews know;
ukjv_translation: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

greek_text: προγινωσκοντες με ανωθεν εαν θελωσιν μαρτυρειν οτι κατα την ακριβεστατην αιρεσιν της ημετερας θρησκειας εζησα φαρισαιος
transliteration: proginwskontev me anwyen ean yelwsin marturein oti kata thn akribestathn airesin thv hmeterav yrhskeiav ezhsa farisaiov
draft_translation: Who knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived as a Pharisee.
ukjv_translation: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

greek_text: και νυν επ ελπιδι της προς τους πατερας επαγγελιας γενομενης υπο του θεου εστηκα κρινομενος
transliteration: kai nun ep elpidi thv prov touv paterav epaggeliav genomenhv upo tou yeou esthka krinomenov
draft_translation: And now I stand being judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers:
ukjv_translation: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God, unto our fathers:

greek_text: εις ην το δωδεκαφυλον ημων εν εκτενεια νυκτα και ημεραν λατρευον ελπιζει καταντησαι περι ης ελπιδος εγκαλουμαι βασιλευ αγριππα υπο των ιουδαιων
transliteration: eiv hn to dwdekafulon hmwn en ekteneia nukta kai hmeran latreuon elpizei katanthsai peri hv elpidov egkaloumai basileu agrippa upo twn ioudaiwn
draft_translation: To which promise our twelve tribes, earnestly serving God night and day, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused by the Jews.
ukjv_translation: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

greek_text: τι απιστον κρινεται παρ υμιν ει ο θεος νεκρους εγειρει
transliteration: ti apiston krinetai par umin ei o yeov nekrouv egeirei
draft_translation: Why is it judged incredible among you, if God raises the dead?
ukjv_translation: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

greek_text: εγω μεν ουν εδοξα εμαυτω προς το ονομα ιησου του ναζωραιου δειν πολλα εναντια πραξαι
transliteration: egw men oun edoxa emautw prov to onoma ihsou tou nazwraiou dein polla enantia praxai
draft_translation: I indeed thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
ukjv_translation: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

greek_text: ο και εποιησα εν ιεροσολυμοις και πολλους των αγιων εγω φυλακαις κατεκλεισα την παρα των αρχιερεων εξουσιαν λαβων αναιρουμενων τε αυτων κατηνεγκα ψηφον
transliteration: o kai epoihsa en ierosolumoiv kai pollouv twn agiwn egw fulakaiv katekleisa thn para twn arcierewn exousian labwn anairoumenwn te autwn kathnegka qhfon
draft_translation: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the holy ones did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
ukjv_translation: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.

greek_text: και κατα πασας τας συναγωγας πολλακις τιμωρων αυτους ηναγκαζον βλασφημειν περισσως τε εμμαινομενος αυτοις εδιωκον εως και εις τας εξω πολεις
transliteration: kai kata pasav tav sunagwgav pollakiv timwrwn autouv hnagkazon blasfhmein perisswv te emmainomenov autoiv ediwkon ewv kai eiv tav exw poleiv
draft_translation: And I punished them often in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
ukjv_translation: And I punished them often in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

greek_text: εν οις και πορευομενος εις την δαμασκον μετ εξουσιας και επιτροπης της παρα των αρχιερεων
transliteration: en oiv kai poreuomenov eiv thn damaskon met exousiav kai epitrophv thv para twn arcierewn
draft_translation: In which also, as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
ukjv_translation: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

greek_text: ημερας μεσης κατα την οδον ειδον βασιλευ ουρανοθεν υπερ την λαμπροτητα του ηλιου περιλαμψαν με φως και τους συν εμοι πορευομενους
transliteration: hmerav meshv kata thn odon eidon basileu ouranoyen uper thn lamprothta tou hliou perilamqan me fwv kai touv sun emoi poreuomenouv
draft_translation: At midday, O king, I saw on the road a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining around me and those who journeyed with me.
ukjv_translation: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

greek_text: παντων δε καταπεσοντων ημων εις την γην ηκουσα φωνην λαλουσαν προς με και λεγουσαν τη εβραιδι διαλεκτω σαουλ σαουλ τι με διωκεις σκληρον σοι προς κεντρα λακτιζειν
transliteration: pantwn de katapesontwn hmwn eiv thn ghn hkousa fwnhn lalousan prov me kai legousan th ebraidi dialektw saoul saoul ti me diwkeiv sklhron soi prov kentra laktizein
draft_translation: And when we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking to me, and saying in the Hebrew dialect, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? it is hard for you to kick against the goads.
ukjv_translation: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me? it is hard for you to kick against the pricks.

greek_text: εγω δε ειπον τις ει κυριε ο δε ειπεν εγω ειμι ιησους ον συ διωκεις
transliteration: egw de eipon tiv ei kurie o de eipen egw eimi ihsouv on su diwkeiv
draft_translation: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom you persecute.
ukjv_translation: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom you persecute.

greek_text: αλλα αναστηθι και στηθι επι τους ποδας σου εις τουτο γαρ ωφθην σοι προχειρισασθαι σε υπηρετην και μαρτυρα ων τε ειδες ων τε οφθησομαι σοι
transliteration: alla anasthyi kai sthyi epi touv podav sou eiv touto gar wfyhn soi proceirisasyai se uphrethn kai martura wn te eidev wn te ofyhsomai soi
draft_translation: But rise, and stand upon your feet: for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to make you a servant and a witness both of these things which you have seen, and of those things in which I will appear to you;
ukjv_translation: But rise, and stand upon your feet: for I have appeared unto you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of these things which you have seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto you;

greek_text: εξαιρουμενος σε εκ του λαου και των εθνων εις ους νυν σε αποστελλω
transliteration: exairoumenov se ek tou laou kai twn eynwn eiv ouv nun se apostellw
draft_translation: Delivering you from the people, and from the nations, to whom now I send you,
ukjv_translation: Delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send you,
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; rendered ethne as nations

greek_text: ανοιξαι οφθαλμους αυτων και επιστρεψαι απο σκοτους εις φως και της εξουσιας του σατανα επι τον θεον του λαβειν αυτους αφεσιν αμαρτιων και κληρον εν τοις ηγιασμενοις πιστει τη εις εμε
transliteration: anoixai ofyalmouv autwn kai epistreqai apo skotouv eiv fwv kai thv exousiav tou satana epi ton yeon tou labein autouv afesin amartiwn kai klhron en toiv hgiasmenoiv pistei th eiv eme
draft_translation: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith that is in me.
ukjv_translation: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized them-which relative

greek_text: οθεν βασιλευ αγριππα ουκ εγενομην απειθης τη ουρανιω οπτασια
transliteration: oyen basileu agrippa ouk egenomhn apeiyhv th ouraniw optasia
draft_translation: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision:
ukjv_translation: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

greek_text: αλλα τοις εν δαμασκω πρωτον και ιεροσολυμοις εις πασαν τε την χωραν της ιουδαιας και τοις εθνεσιν απηγγελλον μετανοειν και επιστρεφειν επι τον θεον αξια της μετανοιας εργα πρασσοντας
transliteration: alla toiv en damaskw prwton kai ierosolumoiv eiv pasan te thn cwran thv ioudaiav kai toiv eynesin aphggellon metanoein kai epistrefein epi ton yeon axia thv metanoiav erga prassontav
draft_translation: But showed first to them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the borders of Judea, and then to the nations, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works worthy of repentance.
ukjv_translation: But showed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; modernized coasts as borders; rendered axios as worthy; rendered ethne as nations; standardized Judea spelling

greek_text: ενεκα τουτων με οι ιουδαιοι συλλαβομενοι εν τω ιερω επειρωντο διαχειρισασθαι
transliteration: eneka toutwn me oi ioudaioi sullabomenoi en tw ierw epeirwnto diaceirisasyai
draft_translation: For these causes the Jews seized me in the temple, and attempted to kill me.
ukjv_translation: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.

greek_text: επικουριας ουν τυχων της παρα του θεου αχρι της ημερας ταυτης εστηκα μαρτυρουμενος μικρω τε και μεγαλω ουδεν εκτος λεγων ων τε οι προφηται ελαλησαν μελλοντων γινεσθαι και μωσης
transliteration: epikouriav oun tucwn thv para tou yeou acri thv hmerav tauthv esthka marturoumenov mikrw te kai megalw ouden ektov legwn wn te oi profhtai elalhsan mellontwn ginesyai kai mwshv
draft_translation: Having therefore obtained help from God, I continue to this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other things than those which the prophets and Moses said would come:
ukjv_translation: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

greek_text: ει παθητος ο χριστος ει πρωτος εξ αναστασεως νεκρων φως μελλει καταγγελλειν τω λαω και τοις εθνεσιν
transliteration: ei payhtov o cristov ei prwtov ex anastasewv nekrwn fwv mellei kataggellein tw law kai toiv eynesin
draft_translation: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should show light to the people, and to the nations.
ukjv_translation: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should show light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; rendered ethne as nations

greek_text: ταυτα δε αυτου απολογουμενου ο φηστος μεγαλη τη φωνη εφη μαινη παυλε τα πολλα σε γραμματα εις μανιαν περιτρεπει
transliteration: tauta de autou apologoumenou o fhstov megalh th fwnh efh mainh paule ta polla se grammata eiv manian peritrepei
draft_translation: And as he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are out of your mind; much learning turns you to madness.
ukjv_translation: And as he thus spoke for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are out of your mind; much learning does make you mad.

greek_text: ο δε ου μαινομαι φησιν κρατιστε φηστε αλλ αληθειας και σωφροσυνης ρηματα αποφθεγγομαι
transliteration: o de ou mainomai fhsin kratiste fhste all alhyeiav kai swfrosunhv rhmata apofyeggomai
draft_translation: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth words of truth and sobriety.
ukjv_translation: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words (o. rhema) of truth and soberness.

greek_text: επισταται γαρ περι τουτων ο βασιλευς προς ον και παρρησιαζομενος λαλω λανθανειν γαρ αυτον τι τουτων ου πειθομαι ουδεν ου γαρ εστιν εν γωνια πεπραγμενον τουτο
transliteration: epistatai gar peri toutwn o basileuv prov on kai parrhsiazomenov lalw lanyanein gar auton ti toutwn ou peiyomai ouden ou gar estin en gwnia pepragmenon touto
draft_translation: For the king knows of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
ukjv_translation: For the king knows of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

greek_text: πιστευεις βασιλευ αγριππα τοις προφηταις οιδα οτι πιστευεις
transliteration: pisteueiv basileu agrippa toiv profhtaiv oida oti pisteueiv
draft_translation: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.
ukjv_translation: King Agrippa, believe you the prophets? I know that you believe.

greek_text: ο δε αγριππας προς τον παυλον εφη εν ολιγω με πειθεις χριστιανον γενεσθαι
transliteration: o de agrippav prov ton paulon efh en oligw me peiyeiv cristianon genesyai
draft_translation: Then Agrippa said to Paul, In a short time you persuade me to become a Christian.
ukjv_translation: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost you persuade me to be a Christian.

greek_text: ο δε παυλος ειπεν ευξαιμην αν τω θεω και εν ολιγω και εν πολλω ου μονον σε αλλα και παντας τους ακουοντας μου σημερον γενεσθαι τοιουτους οποιος καγω ειμι παρεκτος των δεσμων τουτων
transliteration: o de paulov eipen euxaimhn an tw yew kai en oligw kai en pollw ou monon se alla kai pantav touv akouontav mou shmeron genesyai toioutouv opoiov kagw eimi parektov twn desmwn toutwn
draft_translation: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only you, but also all who hear me this day, whether in a little or in much, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.
ukjv_translation: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only you, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

greek_text: και ταυτα ειποντος αυτου ανεστη ο βασιλευς και ο ηγεμων η τε βερνικη και οι συγκαθημενοι αυτοις
transliteration: kai tauta eipontov autou anesth o basileuv kai o hgemwn h te bernikh kai oi sugkayhmenoi autoiv
draft_translation: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them:
ukjv_translation: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

greek_text: και αναχωρησαντες ελαλουν προς αλληλους λεγοντες οτι ουδεν θανατου αξιον η δεσμων πρασσει ο ανθρωπος ουτος
transliteration: kai anacwrhsantev elaloun prov allhlouv legontev oti ouden yanatou axion h desmwn prassei o anyrwpov outov
draft_translation: And when they had gone aside, they talked among themselves, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
ukjv_translation: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

greek_text: αγριππας δε τω φηστω εφη απολελυσθαι εδυνατο ο ανθρωπος ουτος ει μη επεκεκλητο καισαρα
transliteration: agrippav de tw fhstw efh apolelusyai edunato o anyrwpov outov ei mh epekeklhto kaisara
draft_translation: Then Agrippa said to Festus, This man could have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed to Caesar.
ukjv_translation: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.

greek_text: ως δε εκριθη του αποπλειν ημας εις την ιταλιαν παρεδιδουν τον τε παυλον και τινας ετερους δεσμωτας εκατονταρχη ονοματι ιουλιω σπειρης σεβαστης
transliteration: wv de ekriyh tou apoplein hmav eiv thn italian paredidoun ton te paulon kai tinav eterouv desmwtav ekatontarch onomati iouliw speirhv sebasthv
draft_translation: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to one named Julius, a centurion of the Augustan cohort.
ukjv_translation: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.

greek_text: επιβαντες δε πλοιω αδραμυττηνω μελλοντες πλειν τους κατα την ασιαν τοπους ανηχθημεν οντος συν ημιν αρισταρχου μακεδονος θεσσαλονικεως
transliteration: epibantev de ploiw adramutthnw mellontev plein touv kata thn asian topouv anhcyhmen ontov sun hmin aristarcou makedonov yessalonikewv
draft_translation: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we put to sea, intending to sail by the places along Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
ukjv_translation: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

greek_text: τη τε ετερα κατηχθημεν εις σιδωνα φιλανθρωπως τε ο ιουλιος τω παυλω χρησαμενος επετρεψεν προς τους φιλους πορευθεντα επιμελειας τυχειν
transliteration: th te etera kathcyhmen eiv sidwna filanyrwpwv te o iouliov tw paulw crhsamenov epetreqen prov touv filouv poreuyenta epimeleiav tucein
draft_translation: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go to his friends to refresh himself.
ukjv_translation: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

greek_text: κακειθεν αναχθεντες υπεπλευσαμεν την κυπρον δια το τους ανεμους ειναι εναντιους
transliteration: kakeiyen anacyentev upepleusamen thn kupron dia to touv anemouv einai enantiouv
draft_translation: And when we had launched from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
ukjv_translation: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

greek_text: το τε πελαγος το κατα την κιλικιαν και παμφυλιαν διαπλευσαντες κατηλθομεν εις μυρα της λυκιας
transliteration: to te pelagov to kata thn kilikian kai pamfulian diapleusantev kathlyomen eiv mura thv lukiav
draft_translation: And when we had sailed over the sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
ukjv_translation: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

greek_text: κακει ευρων ο εκατονταρχος πλοιον αλεξανδρινον πλεον εις την ιταλιαν ενεβιβασεν ημας εις αυτο
transliteration: kakei eurwn o ekatontarcov ploion alexandrinon pleon eiv thn italian enebibasen hmav eiv auto
draft_translation: And there the centurion found a boat of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us in it.
ukjv_translation: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
review_notes: modernized therein; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: εν ικαναις δε ημεραις βραδυπλοουντες και μολις γενομενοι κατα την κνιδον μη προσεωντος ημας του ανεμου υπεπλευσαμεν την κρητην κατα σαλμωνην
transliteration: en ikanaiv de hmeraiv braduploountev kai moliv genomenoi kata thn knidon mh prosewntov hmav tou anemou upepleusamen thn krhthn kata salmwnhn
draft_translation: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and with difficulty had come opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone;
ukjv_translation: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come opposite to Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, opposite to Salmone;

greek_text: μολις τε παραλεγομενοι αυτην ηλθομεν εις τοπον τινα καλουμενον καλους λιμενας ω εγγυς ην πολις λασαια
transliteration: moliv te paralegomenoi authn hlyomen eiv topon tina kaloumenon kalouv limenav w egguv hn poliv lasaia
draft_translation: And, with difficulty passing it, came to a place which is called Fair Havens; near to which was the city of Lasea.
ukjv_translation: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh unto which was the city of Lasea.

greek_text: ικανου δε χρονου διαγενομενου και οντος ηδη επισφαλους του πλοος δια το και την νηστειαν ηδη παρεληλυθεναι παρηνει ο παυλος
transliteration: ikanou de cronou diagenomenou kai ontov hdh episfalouv tou ploov dia to kai thn nhsteian hdh parelhluyenai parhnei o paulov
draft_translation: Now when much time had passed, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was already past, Paul admonished them,
ukjv_translation: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,

greek_text: λεγων αυτοις ανδρες θεωρω οτι μετα υβρεως και πολλης ζημιας ου μονον του φορτου και του πλοιου αλλα και των ψυχων ημων μελλειν εσεσθαι τον πλουν
transliteration: legwn autoiv andrev yewrw oti meta ubrewv kai pollhv zhmiav ou monon tou fortou kai tou ploiou alla kai twn qucwn hmwn mellein esesyai ton ploun
draft_translation: And said to them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and boat, but also of our lives.
ukjv_translation: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
review_notes: modernized archaic directional unto; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: ο δε εκατονταρχος τω κυβερνητη και τω ναυκληρω επειθετο μαλλον η τοις υπο του παυλου λεγομενοις
transliteration: o de ekatontarcov tw kubernhth kai tw nauklhrw epeiyeto mallon h toiv upo tou paulou legomenoiv
draft_translation: Nevertheless the centurion believed the pilot and the owner of the ship, more than the things which were spoken by Paul.
ukjv_translation: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

greek_text: ανευθετου δε του λιμενος υπαρχοντος προς παραχειμασιαν οι πλειους εθεντο βουλην αναχθηναι κακειθεν ειπως δυναιντο καταντησαντες εις φοινικα παραχειμασαι λιμενα της κρητης βλεποντα κατα λιβα και κατα χωρον
transliteration: aneuyetou de tou limenov uparcontov prov paraceimasian oi pleiouv eyento boulhn anacyhnai kakeiyen eipwv dunainto katanthsantev eiv foinika paraceimasai limena thv krhthv bleponta kata liba kai kata cwron
draft_translation: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, most advised to depart from there also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is a haven of Crete, and lies toward the south west and north west.
ukjv_translation: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lies toward the south west and north west.
review_notes: modernized article before h-word; modernized more-part idiom; modernized thence

greek_text: υποπνευσαντος δε νοτου δοξαντες της προθεσεως κεκρατηκεναι αραντες ασσον παρελεγοντο την κρητην
transliteration: upopneusantov de notou doxantev thv proyesewv kekrathkenai arantev asson parelegonto thn krhthn
draft_translation: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, weighing anchor, they sailed close by Crete.
ukjv_translation: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

greek_text: μετ ου πολυ δε εβαλεν κατ αυτης ανεμος τυφωνικος ο καλουμενος ευροκλυδων
transliteration: met ou polu de ebalen kat authv anemov tufwnikov o kaloumenov eurokludwn
draft_translation: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
ukjv_translation: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

greek_text: συναρπασθεντος δε του πλοιου και μη δυναμενου αντοφθαλμειν τω ανεμω επιδοντες εφερομεθα
transliteration: sunarpasyentov de tou ploiou kai mh dunamenou antofyalmein tw anemw epidontev eferomeya
draft_translation: And when the boat was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
ukjv_translation: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.

greek_text: νησιον δε τι υποδραμοντες καλουμενον κλαυδην μολις ισχυσαμεν περικρατεις γενεσθαι της σκαφης
transliteration: nhsion de ti upodramontev kaloumenon klaudhn moliv iscusamen perikrateiv genesyai thv skafhv
draft_translation: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much difficulty securing the skiff:
ukjv_translation: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

greek_text: ην αραντες βοηθειαις εχρωντο υποζωννυντες το πλοιον φοβουμενοι τε μη εις την συρτιν εκπεσωσιν χαλασαντες το σκευος ουτως εφεροντο
transliteration: hn arantev bohyeiaiv ecrwnto upozwnnuntev to ploion foboumenoi te mh eiv thn surtin ekpeswsin calasantev to skeuov outwv eferonto
draft_translation: Which when they had taken up, they used support cables, undergirding the boat; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksand, strake sail, and so were driven.
ukjv_translation: Which when they had taken up, they used support cables, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksand, strake sail, and so were driven.

greek_text: σφοδρως δε χειμαζομενων ημων τη εξης εκβολην εποιουντο
transliteration: sfodrwv de ceimazomenwn hmwn th exhv ekbolhn epoiounto
draft_translation: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they jettisoned cargo;
ukjv_translation: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

greek_text: και τη τριτη αυτοχειρες την σκευην του πλοιου ερριψαμεν
transliteration: kai th trith autoceirev thn skeuhn tou ploiou erriqamen
draft_translation: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the cordage of the boat.
ukjv_translation: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the cordage of the ship.

greek_text: μητε δε ηλιου μητε αστρων επιφαινοντων επι πλειονας ημερας χειμωνος τε ουκ ολιγου επικειμενου λοιπον περιηρειτο πασα ελπις του σωζεσθαι ημας
transliteration: mhte de hliou mhte astrwn epifainontwn epi pleionav hmerav ceimwnov te ouk oligou epikeimenou loipon perihreito pasa elpiv tou swzesyai hmav
draft_translation: And when neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
ukjv_translation: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

greek_text: πολλης δε ασιτιας υπαρχουσης τοτε σταθεις ο παυλος εν μεσω αυτων ειπεν εδει μεν ω ανδρες πειθαρχησαντας μοι μη αναγεσθαι απο της κρητης κερδησαι τε την υβριν ταυτην και την ζημιαν
transliteration: pollhv de asitiav uparcoushv tote stayeiv o paulov en mesw autwn eipen edei men w andrev peiyarchsantav moi mh anagesyai apo thv krhthv kerdhsai te thn ubrin tauthn kai thn zhmian
draft_translation: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Men, you should have listened to me, and not have sailed from Crete, and incurred this harm and loss.
ukjv_translation: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, all of you should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

greek_text: και τα νυν παραινω υμας ευθυμειν αποβολη γαρ ψυχης ουδεμια εσται εξ υμων πλην του πλοιου
transliteration: kai ta nun parainw umav euyumein apobolh gar quchv oudemia estai ex umwn plhn tou ploiou
draft_translation: And now I exhort you to take courage: for there shall be no loss of anyone's life among you, but of the boat.
ukjv_translation: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.
review_notes: modernized any-man idiom; modernized good-cheer idiom; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: παρεστη γαρ μοι τη νυκτι ταυτη αγγελος του θεου ου ειμι ω και λατρευω
transliteration: paresth gar moi th nukti tauth aggelov tou yeou ou eimi w kai latreuw
draft_translation: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
ukjv_translation: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

greek_text: λεγων μη φοβου παυλε καισαρι σε δει παραστηναι και ιδου κεχαρισται σοι ο θεος παντας τους πλεοντας μετα σου
transliteration: legwn mh fobou paule kaisari se dei parasthnai kai idou kecaristai soi o yeov pantav touv pleontav meta sou
draft_translation: Saying, Do not fear, Paul; you must be brought before Caesar: and, look, God has given you all those who sail with you.
ukjv_translation: Saying, Fear not, Paul; you must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God has given you all them that sail with you.

greek_text: διο ευθυμειτε ανδρες πιστευω γαρ τω θεω οτι ουτως εσται καθ ον τροπον λελαληται μοι
transliteration: dio euyumeite andrev pisteuw gar tw yew oti outwv estai kay on tropon lelalhtai moi
draft_translation: Therefore, men, take courage: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
ukjv_translation: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

greek_text: εις νησον δε τινα δει ημας εκπεσειν
transliteration: eiv nhson de tina dei hmav ekpesein
draft_translation: Nevertheless we must be cast upon a certain island.
ukjv_translation: Nevertheless we must be cast upon a certain island.

greek_text: ως δε τεσσαρεσκαιδεκατη νυξ εγενετο διαφερομενων ημων εν τω αδρια κατα μεσον της νυκτος υπενοουν οι ναυται προσαγειν τινα αυτοις χωραν
transliteration: wv de tessareskaidekath nux egeneto diaferomenwn hmwn en tw adria kata meson thv nuktov upenooun oi nautai prosagein tina autoiv cwran
draft_translation: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven up and down in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors supposed that they were drawing near to some land;
ukjv_translation: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the sailors deemed that they drew near to some country;

greek_text: και βολισαντες ευρον οργυιας εικοσι βραχυ δε διαστησαντες και παλιν βολισαντες ευρον οργυιας δεκαπεντε
transliteration: kai bolisantev euron orguiav eikosi bracu de diasthsantev kai palin bolisantev euron orguiav dekapente
draft_translation: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
ukjv_translation: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

greek_text: φοβουμενοι τε μηπως εις τραχεις τοπους εκπεσωμεν εκ πρυμνης ριψαντες αγκυρας τεσσαρας ηυχοντο ημεραν γενεσθαι
transliteration: foboumenoi te mhpwv eiv traceiv topouv ekpeswmen ek prumnhv riqantev agkurav tessarav huconto hmeran genesyai
draft_translation: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rough places, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
ukjv_translation: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

greek_text: των δε ναυτων ζητουντων φυγειν εκ του πλοιου και χαλασαντων την σκαφην εις την θαλασσαν προφασει ως εκ πρωρας μελλοντων αγκυρας εκτεινειν
transliteration: twn de nautwn zhtountwn fugein ek tou ploiou kai calasantwn thn skafhn eiv thn yalassan profasei wv ek prwrav mellontwn agkurav ekteinein
draft_translation: And as the sailors were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under pretense as though they would have cast anchors out of the bow,
ukjv_translation: And as the sailors were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the bow,

greek_text: ειπεν ο παυλος τω εκατονταρχη και τοις στρατιωταις εαν μη ουτοι μεινωσιν εν τω πλοιω υμεις σωθηναι ου δυνασθε
transliteration: eipen o paulov tw ekatontarch kai toiv stratiwtaiv ean mh outoi meinwsin en tw ploiw umeiv swyhnai ou dunasye
draft_translation: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Unless these remain in the ship, you cannot be saved.
ukjv_translation: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, all of you cannot be saved.

greek_text: τοτε οι στρατιωται απεκοψαν τα σχοινια της σκαφης και ειασαν αυτην εκπεσειν
transliteration: tote oi stratiwtai apekoqan ta scoinia thv skafhv kai eiasan authn ekpesein
draft_translation: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the skiff, and let it fall away.
ukjv_translation: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

greek_text: αχρι δε ου εμελλεν ημερα γινεσθαι παρεκαλει ο παυλος απαντας μεταλαβειν τροφης λεγων τεσσαρεσκαιδεκατην σημερον ημεραν προσδοκωντες ασιτοι διατελειτε μηδεν προσλαβομενοι
transliteration: acri de ou emellen hmera ginesyai parekalei o paulov apantav metalabein trofhv legwn tessareskaidekathn shmeron hmeran prosdokwntev asitoi diateleite mhden proslabomenoi
draft_translation: And while the day was coming on, Paul urged them all to take food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that you have waited and continued without food, having taken nothing.
ukjv_translation: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that all of you have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

greek_text: διο παρακαλω υμας προσλαβειν τροφης τουτο γαρ προς της υμετερας σωτηριας υπαρχει ουδενος γαρ υμων θριξ εκ της κεφαλης πεσειται
transliteration: dio parakalw umav proslabein trofhv touto gar prov thv umeterav swthriav uparcei oudenov gar umwn yrix ek thv kefalhv peseitai
draft_translation: Therefore I ask you to take some food: for this is for your health: for there shall not a hair fall from the head of any of you.
ukjv_translation: Wherefore I pray you to take some food: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
review_notes: modernized I-pray-you wording; modernized article before h-word; modernized wherefore

greek_text: ειπων δε ταυτα και λαβων αρτον ευχαριστησεν τω θεω ενωπιον παντων και κλασας ηρξατο εσθιειν
transliteration: eipwn de tauta kai labwn arton eucaristhsen tw yew enwpion pantwn kai klasav hrxato esyiein
draft_translation: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in the presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
ukjv_translation: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.

greek_text: ευθυμοι δε γενομενοι παντες και αυτοι προσελαβοντο τροφης
transliteration: euyumoi de genomenoi pantev kai autoi proselabonto trofhv
draft_translation: Then they were all encouraged, and also took food.
ukjv_translation: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some food.

greek_text: ημεν δε εν τω πλοιω αι πασαι ψυχαι διακοσιαι εβδομηκονταεξ
transliteration: hmen de en tw ploiw ai pasai qucai diakosiai ebdomhkontaex
draft_translation: And we were in all in the ship 276 souls.
ukjv_translation: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

greek_text: κορεσθεντες δε τροφης εκουφιζον το πλοιον εκβαλλομενοι τον σιτον εις την θαλασσαν
transliteration: koresyentev de trofhv ekoufizon to ploion ekballomenoi ton siton eiv thn yalassan
draft_translation: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the boat, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
ukjv_translation: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

greek_text: οτε δε ημερα εγενετο την γην ουκ επεγινωσκον κολπον δε τινα κατενοουν εχοντα αιγιαλον εις ον εβουλευσαντο ει δυναιντο εξωσαι το πλοιον
transliteration: ote de hmera egeneto thn ghn ouk epeginwskon kolpon de tina katenooun econta aigialon eiv on ebouleusanto ei dunainto exwsai to ploion
draft_translation: And when it was day, they did not know the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the boat.
ukjv_translation: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
review_notes: modernized knew-not idiom; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: και τας αγκυρας περιελοντες ειων εις την θαλασσαν αμα ανεντες τας ζευκτηριας των πηδαλιων και επαραντες τον αρτεμονα τη πνεουση κατειχον εις τον αιγιαλον
transliteration: kai tav agkurav perielontev eiwn eiv thn yalassan ama anentev tav zeukthriav twn phdaliwn kai eparantev ton artemona th pneoush kateicon eiv ton aigialon
draft_translation: And when they had cut away the anchors, they left them in the sea, and at the same time loosed the rudder bands, and hoisted the foresail to the wind, and made toward shore.
ukjv_translation: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoisted up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

greek_text: περιπεσοντες δε εις τοπον διθαλασσον επωκειλαν την ναυν και η μεν πρωρα ερεισασα εμεινεν ασαλευτος η δε πρυμνα ελυετο υπο της βιας των κυματων
transliteration: peripesontev de eiv topon diyalasson epwkeilan thn naun kai h men prwra ereisasa emeinen asaleutov h de prumna elueto upo thv biav twn kumatwn
draft_translation: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the front part stuck fast, and remained immovable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
ukjv_translation: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the front part stuck fast, and remained immoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

greek_text: των δε στρατιωτων βουλη εγενετο ινα τους δεσμωτας αποκτεινωσιν μη τις εκκολυμβησας διαφυγοι
transliteration: twn de stratiwtwn boulh egeneto ina touv desmwtav apokteinwsin mh tiv ekkolumbhsav diafugoi
draft_translation: And the soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.
ukjv_translation: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

greek_text: ο δε εκατονταρχος βουλομενος διασωσαι τον παυλον εκωλυσεν αυτους του βουληματος εκελευσεν τε τους δυναμενους κολυμβαν απορριψαντας πρωτους επι την γην εξιεναι
transliteration: o de ekatontarcov boulomenov diaswsai ton paulon ekwlusen autouv tou boulhmatov ekeleusen te touv dunamenouv kolumban aporriqantav prwtouv epi thn ghn exienai
draft_translation: But the centurion, wanting to save Paul, prevented them from their purpose; and commanded that those who could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
ukjv_translation: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:

greek_text: και τους λοιπους ους μεν επι σανισιν ους δε επι τινων των απο του πλοιου και ουτως εγενετο παντας διασωθηναι επι την γην
transliteration: kai touv loipouv ouv men epi sanisin ouv de epi tinwn twn apo tou ploiou kai outwv egeneto pantav diaswyhnai epi thn ghn
draft_translation: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the boat. And so it happened, that they escaped all safe to land.
ukjv_translation: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
review_notes: modernized came-to-pass idiom; rendered ploion as boat

greek_text: και διασωθεντες τοτε επεγνωσαν οτι μελιτη η νησος καλειται
transliteration: kai diaswyentev tote epegnwsan oti melith h nhsov kaleitai
draft_translation: And when they had escaped, then they knew that the island was called Malta.
ukjv_translation: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

greek_text: οι δε βαρβαροι παρειχον ου την τυχουσαν φιλανθρωπιαν ημιν αναψαντες γαρ πυραν προσελαβοντο παντας ημας δια τον υετον τον εφεστωτα και δια το ψυχος
transliteration: oi de barbaroi pareicon ou thn tucousan filanyrwpian hmin anaqantev gar puran proselabonto pantav hmav dia ton ueton ton efestwta kai dia to qucov
draft_translation: And the islanders showed us no ordinary kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
ukjv_translation: And the natives people showed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

greek_text: συστρεψαντος δε του παυλου φρυγανων πληθος και επιθεντος επι την πυραν εχιδνα εκ της θερμης εξελθουσα καθηψεν της χειρος αυτου
transliteration: sustreqantov de tou paulou fruganwn plhyov kai epiyentov epi thn puran ecidna ek thv yermhv exelyousa kayhqen thv ceirov autou
draft_translation: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
ukjv_translation: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

greek_text: ως δε ειδον οι βαρβαροι κρεμαμενον το θηριον εκ της χειρος αυτου ελεγον προς αλληλους παντως φονευς εστιν ο ανθρωπος ουτος ον διασωθεντα εκ της θαλασσης η δικη ζην ουκ ειασεν
transliteration: wv de eidon oi barbaroi kremamenon to yhrion ek thv ceirov autou elegon prov allhlouv pantwv foneuv estin o anyrwpov outov on diaswyenta ek thv yalasshv h dikh zhn ouk eiasen
draft_translation: And when the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said among themselves, Certainly this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, Justice has not allowed to live.
ukjv_translation: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffers not to live.
